prior_art_notes: Mordatch-Todorov-Popović 2012 SIGGRAPH is the canonical academic disclosure of contact-invariant optimization for humanoid motion synthesis. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) treating contact existence and contact forces as continuous optimization variables rather than combinatorial mode switches — directly relevant to modern claims on contact-implicit humanoid trajectory optimization (Posa-Tedrake 2014, Manchester 2017, Mastalli 2020 Crocoddyl all build on this); (2) automatic contact-sequence discovery in humanoid locomotion and manipulation — anticipates patents on adaptive footstep planning and automatic grasp placement for humanoid IP; (3) the unified trajectory-optimization formulation that synthesizes diverse behaviors (walking, climbing, getup, manipulation) in a single framework — relevant to claims on multi-task humanoid motion synthesis. SIGGRAPH 2012 paper has >1000 citations and is foundational in both robotics and computer animation. Modern contact-implicit humanoid trajectory optimization IP faces this 14-year-deep academic anchor.
sources: Mordatch, I.; Todorov, E.; Popović, Z. 'Discovery of Complex Behaviors through Contact-Invariant Optimization.' ACM TOG 31(4), Article 43 (SIGGRAPH 2012). DOI: 10.1145/2185520.2185539.
Mordatch, I.; Wang, J.; Todorov, E.; Popović, Z. 'Animating Human Lower Limbs Using Contact-Invariant Optimization.' ACM TOG (SIGGRAPH Asia 2013).
Posa, M.; Cantu, C.; Tedrake, R. 'A direct method for trajectory optimization of rigid bodies through contact.' IJRR 33(1), 2014 (closely related contact-implicit method).

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, demonstrated on simulated MuJoCo humanoid (28-DoF), swimmer, and cheetah models. Iterative Linear Quadratic Gaussian (iLQG) — a differential-dynamic-programming-class trajectory optimizer that linearizes the dynamics about a nominal trajectory and solves a sequence of LQG subproblems with regularization. Receding-horizon online application enables real-time MPC at >100 Hz on 28-DoF humanoid models. The 2012 paper introduces the regularization scheme and line search that made iLQG run online.
aliases: Synthesis and Stabilization of Complex Behaviors through Online Trajectory Optimization
canonical_name: Tassa iLQG / Synthesis and Stabilization of Complex Behaviors
control_architecture: Online receding-horizon trajectory optimization (model-predictive control) via iLQG. Computes locally optimal feedback policies in addition to feedforward trajectories — i.e., the algorithm produces both u(t) and a time-varying gain K(t), giving stabilizing closed-loop control. Demonstrated humanoid getup, walking, and recovery from disturbances in MuJoCo simulation.
creator: Yuval Tassa, Tom Erez, Emanuel Todorov; Department of Computer Science and Engineering, University of Washington (Todorov lab)
disclosure_citation: Tassa, Yuval; Erez, Tom; Todorov, Emanuel. 'Synthesis and Stabilization of Complex Behaviors through Online Trajectory Optimization.' IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), Vilamoura, Portugal, October 2012, pp. 4906-4913. DOI: 10.1109/IROS.2012.6386025. Earlier: Tassa, Y.; Erez, T.; Smart, W.D. 'Receding Horizon Differential Dynamic Programming.' NeurIPS 2007. Foundational underlying method: Li, W. and Todorov, E. 'Iterative linear quadratic regulator design for nonlinear biological movement systems.' ICINCO 2004.
end_effector: generic; demonstrated on multi-body simulated humanoid
notable_capabilities: online iLQG trajectory optimization for 28-DoF humanoid in MuJoCo
humanoid getup, walking, recovery synthesized without hand-designed gait library
feedback policy synthesized jointly with feedforward
prior_art_notes: Tassa-Erez-Todorov 2012 IROS is the canonical academic disclosure of online iLQG-based model-predictive control for high-DoF humanoid systems. Anticipates with full mathematical specificity: (1) online receding-horizon trajectory optimization for 28-DoF humanoid models at real-time rates — directly relevant to claims on humanoid MPC IP (Boston Dynamics, Apptronik, Figure, Tesla all employ trajectory-optimization-class controllers); (2) the regularization-and-line-search scheme that enabled iLQG to run online with stable convergence — anticipates implementation-detail patents on regularized DDP/iLQG humanoid controllers; (3) jointly synthesizing feedforward trajectories AND time-varying feedback gains — relevant to claims on closed-loop humanoid trajectory IP. Open-source MuJoCo code release accompanies the paper (the foundational MuJoCo iLQG demo). Modern humanoid trajectory-optimization MPC IP faces this 14-year-deep academic anchor with full implementation disclosure. Foundational lineage: Li-Todorov ICINCO 2004 (iLQR primitive); Jacobson-Mayne 1970 (DDP); Bellman 1957 (dynamic programming). Direct downstream: every major modern humanoid MPC stack.
sensing: simulated full-state observation; algorithm-agnostic to real-sensor pipelines
sources: Tassa, Y.; Erez, T.; Todorov, E. 'Synthesis and Stabilization of Complex Behaviors through Online Trajectory Optimization.' IROS 2012: 4906-4913. DOI: 10.1109/IROS.2012.6386025.
Li, W. and Todorov, E. 'Iterative linear quadratic regulator design for nonlinear biological movement systems.' ICINCO 2004 (foundational iLQR).
Tassa, Y.; Mansard, N.; Todorov, E. 'Control-Limited Differential Dynamic Programming.' ICRA 2014 (constrained extension).

actuator_details: Physics simulation engine optimized for model-based control: stable contact dynamics, fast forward + inverse dynamics, smooth analytical derivatives. Designed expressly for the iLQG / MPC use case (Tassa iLQG 2012 entry uses MuJoCo). The dominant academic simulator for humanoid and manipulator policy training since the mid-2010s.
control_architecture: Provides simulation substrate for arbitrary control architectures. Standard MJCF model format; Python (mujoco) and C bindings.
creator: Emo Todorov, Tom Erez, Yuval Tassa (originally University of Washington / Roboti LLC; now Google DeepMind)
disclosure_citation: Todorov, E., Erez, T., Tassa, Y. 'MuJoCo: A physics engine for model-based control'. IROS 2012. Originally proprietary (Roboti LLC); acquired by Google DeepMind October 2021 and released under Apache-2.0.
notable_capabilities: MJCF model format (which OpenLoco compiles to)
the substrate for thousands of robotics RL/MPC papers
prior_art_notes: MuJoCo is the canonical academic physics engine for model-based robotic control (Todorov-Erez-Tassa 2012). 13-year-deep prior art spanning the proprietary Roboti era (2012-2021) and the open-source DeepMind era (2021+). The substrate that the Tassa iLQG entry, Howell-Tassa MuJoCo MPC entry, MJX entry, and Genesis simulator entry all build on or interop with. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on contact-rich policy training simulation. MJCF is the format OpenLoco compiles to, so MuJoCo is the reference simulator for the entire free-humanoid-family.
sensing: simulated cameras, IMUs, joint sensors, force/torque

actuator_details: Series-elastic actuators throughout; rotary and linear
control_architecture: IHMC-derived whole-body control; ROS-based
creator: NASA Johnson Space Center, in collaboration with University of Texas at Austin and others
disclosure_citation: NASA Johnson Space Center, DARPA Robotics Challenge entry, 2013.
notes: Among the most thoroughly published private-but-open humanoid platforms.
prior_art_notes: NASA Valkyrie's series-elastic actuator implementations and the IHMC-derived whole-body control work are foundational prior art. The robot was distributed to multiple universities and produced extensive open publications.
sources: Radford, N. et al. 'Valkyrie: NASA's First Bipedal Humanoid Robot.' Journal of Field Robotics 32(3), 2015.

actuator_details: Series-elastic actuators with fiberglass leaf-spring legs implementing the spring-loaded inverted pendulum (SLIP) model
control_architecture: reduced-order spring-mass model; SLIP-based control
creator: Oregon State University, Dynamic Robotics Laboratory (Jonathan Hurst)
disclosure_citation: Hubicki, C. et al. 'ATRIAS: Design and validation of a tether-free 3D-capable spring-mass bipedal robot.' International Journal of Robotics Research 35(12), 2016.
ip_citations: academic publication; OSU patents licensed widely
notable_capabilities: first machine to walk in 3D space using passive-dynamics-inspired control
demonstrated robust unscripted human-like walking gaits
notes: Direct ancestor of Cassie which became the basis for Agility Robotics' Digit. The Hurst-lab academic chain is among the most-cited in modern bipedal robotics.
prior_art_notes: ATRIAS is foundational prior art for spring-mass bipedal locomotion. The SLIP-based reduced-order control approach has become a dominant paradigm in dynamic bipedal walking, anticipating many subsequent commercial control claims.
sources: Hurst, J. et al. various IROS and ICRA publications, 2012-2015.

actuator_details: First-generation high-torque electric actuators with custom motor design
control_architecture: energy-efficient legged locomotion control
creator: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab (Sangbae Kim)
disclosure_citation: Seok, S. et al. 'Design principles for energy-efficient legged locomotion and implementation on the MIT Cheetah robot.' IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics 20(3), 2015. Earlier ICRA 2013 disclosure.
notes: Sometimes referred to as 'Cheetah 1'; the lab numbering is informal. Direct ancestor of all subsequent MIT Cheetah-family designs.
prior_art_notes: First-generation MIT Cheetah established the design principles for high-torque electric quadrupeds. Seok 2015 T-Mech paper provides foundational design-principles disclosure that anticipates many subsequent legged-robot actuation claims.
sources: Seok, S. et al. IEEE/ASME T-Mech 20(3), 2015.

actuator_details: Framework demonstrated on Sarcos Slave Arm, ATRIAS, ASIMO-class simulators, Barrett WAM. Discrete and rhythmic DMPs disclosed in canonical second-order ODE form: τż = αz(βz(g − y) − z) + f(x), with phase variable x and forcing term f(x) parameterized by Gaussian basis weights learned from demonstration.
control_architecture: dynamical-system attractor model with phase-coupled forcing term; supports discrete (point-attractor) and rhythmic (limit-cycle) primitives, online goal modulation, and obstacle-avoidance via coupling terms. Provably stable convergence; closed-form per-DOF formulation.
creator: Auke Ijspeert, Stefan Schaal, Jun Nakanishi, Heiko Hoffmann, Peter Pastor
disclosure_citation: Ijspeert, Auke Jan, Nakanishi, Jun, Hoffmann, Heiko, Pastor, Peter, Schaal, Stefan. 'Dynamical Movement Primitives: Learning Attractor Models for Motor Behaviors.' Neural Computation 25(2): 328-373, February 2013. Earlier foundations: Schaal, S., Peters, J., Nakanishi, J., Ijspeert, A. 'Learning movement primitives.' International Symposium on Robotics Research (ISRR) 2003; Schaal, Mohajerian, Ijspeert. 'Dynamics systems vs. optimal control — a unifying view.' Progress in Brain Research 165: 425-445, 2007.
prior_art_notes: Ijspeert-Schaal DMPs are the canonical academic disclosure of learnable, stable, parameterized motor primitives for robotic motion generation. The 2013 Neural Computation paper consolidates the formal framework; the 2007 Progress in Brain Research extension and the 2002-2003 Schaal/Ijspeert papers establish lineage. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on demonstration-learned humanoid motion primitives with online goal modulation — DMPs disclose the closed-form ODE structure used in essentially every humanoid skill-library paper since 2007; (2) claims on rhythmic locomotion primitives with phase coupling — directly anticipates pattern-generator humanoid IP; (3) claims on obstacle-avoiding modulated motion primitives — the coupling-term extension is explicit in the 2013 paper. >5000 citations; broadly available through open Neural Computation archives. Modern humanoid skill-primitive IP filings face this lineage at 13-23 years' depth.
sources: Ijspeert, A. J., Nakanishi, J., Hoffmann, H., Pastor, P., Schaal, S. 'Dynamical Movement Primitives.' Neural Computation 25(2): 328-373, 2013.
Schaal, S., Mohajerian, P., Ijspeert, A. 'Dynamics systems vs. optimal control.' Prog. Brain Res. 165: 425-445, 2007.
Ijspeert, A. J., Nakanishi, J., Schaal, S. 'Movement imitation with nonlinear dynamical systems.' IEEE ICRA 2002.

actuator_details: Six-legged sprawl-tuned crawling robot (~75 g class). Single brushless DC motor drives a four-bar mechanism that produces alternating tripod leg motion. **Sprawl angle is mechanically tunable** between flat (legs splayed wide) and tall (legs pulled in) configurations to adapt to different terrains and obstacle types. PCB-process-fabricated linkage frames; passive compliance via flexible polymer.
control_architecture: Open-loop alternating-tripod gait; sprawl angle is mechanically set per terrain. Pre-programmed mission patterns; no real-time adaptation.
creator: UC Berkeley Biomimetic Millisystems Lab; Ronald Fearing group; Kohut, Karras, et al.
disclosure_citation: Karras, J. T., Fuller, C. L., Carpenter, K. C., Buscicchio, A., McKeeby, D., Norris, C. J., Parcheta, C. E., Royal, M. I., Wilcox, B. H., Fearing, R. S. 'Climbing with sprawl-tuned autonomous robots'. (Original Kohut/Fearing STAR variants 2010-2013.) IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) 2013. UC Berkeley Biomimetic Millisystems Lab.
notable_capabilities: 5 m/s top speed (10× body-length per second)
mechanical sprawl tuning for terrain adaptation
prior_art_notes: STAR is the original sprawl-tuned reconfigurable miniature robot from the Fearing group at Berkeley. 13-year open-academic publication record. Establishes the 'sprawl-tuned wheel-leg-hybrid + four-bar mechanism' architectural pattern that the entire STAR family (RSTAR, TSTAR, FSTAR, FCSTAR, AmphiSTAR, DSTAR) descends from. Directly shields free-humanoid-centaur's wheel-leg-hybrid commitment and any commercial claim on compact reconfigurable-mechanism wheel-leg robotics.
sensing: bump-switch contact sensors (some variants); minimal onboard sensing — relies on mechanical adaptation
sources: Kohut, N. J., Birkmeyer, P. M., Peterson, K. C., Fearing, R. S. 'Maneuverability and mobility in palm-sized legged robots'. SPIE 8389 2012.

actuator_details: Compact compliant quadruped, 1.1 kg, 21 cm body length. Servo-actuated hip joint per leg, passive compliant foot via pantograph mechanism with parallel spring. Open-source design.
control_architecture: central pattern generator (Ijspeert-lineage) with parameterized gait coordination; bottom-up bio-inspired locomotion control
creator: Spröwitz, Tuleu, Vespignani, Ajallooeian, Badri, Ijspeert; EPFL Biorobotics Laboratory
disclosure_citation: Spröwitz, A., Tuleu, A., Vespignani, M., Ajallooeian, M., Badri, E., Ijspeert, A.J. 'Towards dynamic trot gait locomotion: Design, control, and experiments with Cheetah-cub, a compliant quadruped robot'. International Journal of Robotics Research 32(8): 932-950, December 2013.
prior_art_notes: Cheetah-cub is one of the earliest open-source compliant compact quadruped academic disclosures. Anticipates: (1) compact open-source compliant quadruped — directly relevant to modern claims on small commercial quadrupeds (Unitree Go1, Boston Dynamics Spot Mini class); (2) parametric CPG-based gait control on a real platform — relevant to bio-inspired locomotion claims; (3) pantograph-leg mechanism as a compliant-footed quadruped architecture — relevant to compliant-leg quadruped IP. The 2013 IJRR paper and open-source EPFL releases provide deep prior art for modern commercial compact quadrupeds.
sources: Spröwitz, A. et al. 'Towards dynamic trot gait locomotion'. IJRR 32(8), 2013.
EPFL Biorobotics Laboratory public design files (2013-2018).

actuator_details: Quasi-direct-drive proprioceptive actuators (foundational implementation)
control_architecture: impulse-based bounding control
creator: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab (Sangbae Kim)
disclosure_citation: Park, H.-W. et al. 'High-speed bounding with the MIT Cheetah 2: Control design and experiments.' International Journal of Robotics Research 36(2), 2017. Earlier ICRA disclosure 2014.
ip_citations: MIT academic publications; Wensing 2017 T-RO paper on actuator design
notes: Original MIT Cheetah (1) was hydraulic; Cheetah 2 transitioned to electric QDD which became the architectural standard.
prior_art_notes: MIT Cheetah 2 establishes the QDD actuator topology in a working high-speed legged robot. The Wensing 2017 T-RO paper 'Proprioceptive actuator design in the MIT Cheetah' is the foundational actuator design disclosure.
sources: Wensing, P.M. et al. 'Proprioceptive actuator design in the MIT Cheetah.' IEEE T-RO 33(3), 2017.

actuator_details: Bimanual Barrett WAM 7-DoF arms on a Segway RMP-200 holonomic mobile base; Barrett BH-280 three-finger underactuated hands. Andy successor platform extended with omnidirectional drive and dual force-torque wrists. Compliant joints via cable-driven WAM transmission with passive backdrivability.
canonical_name: CMU Personal Robotics Lab Andy / HERB-2 follow-on platform
control_architecture: OpenRAVE planning stack with CHOMP/STOMP trajectory optimization, TSR (task-space-region) constraint encoding, and shared-autonomy policy blending (Dragan-Srinivasa 2013) — formal mathematical framework for arbitrating between operator and autonomous policy.
creator: Siddhartha Srinivasa, Anca Dragan, J. Andrew Bagnell, and the CMU Personal Robotics Lab
disclosure_citation: Srinivasa, Siddhartha S. et al. 'HERB 2.0: Lessons Learned from Developing a Mobile Manipulator for the Home.' Proceedings of the IEEE, vol. 100, no. 8, 2012; subsequent Andy disclosures: Dragan, Anca and Srinivasa, S. 'A Policy-Blending Formalism for Shared Control.' IJRR 32(7), 2013; Bagnell et al. CHIMP/Andy whole-body manipulation reports 2013-2015.
notable_capabilities: bimanual mobile manipulation in unstructured home environments
prior_art_notes: The Andy / HERB-2 generation extends HERB-1 with formal shared-autonomy theory and is the survey-of-record for bimanual mobile-manipulator home robots in 2012-2015. It anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on shared-autonomy arbitration between operator and policy — Dragan-Srinivasa policy-blending IJRR 2013 publishes the closed-form linear arbitration in confidence space; (2) claims on task-space-region constraint encoding for manipulation planning — Berenson-Srinivasa-Kuffner ICRA 2009 publishes TSR formalism executed on this platform; (3) claims on underactuated cable-driven grasping for unstructured pick-and-place — Barrett BH-280 deployment is the canonical published baseline. Modern humanoid manipulation IP claiming shared-autonomy or constraint-region planning faces these timestamped CMU disclosures.
sensing: head-mounted Kinect/PrimeSense depth, Barrett strain-gauge fingertip force, wrist 6-axis force-torque, encoder proprioception
sources: Srinivasa, S. et al. 'HERB 2.0' Proc. IEEE 100(8), 2012.
Dragan, A. and Srinivasa, S. 'A Policy-Blending Formalism for Shared Control.' IJRR 32(7), 2013.
Berenson, D., Srinivasa, S., Kuffner, J. 'Task Space Regions: A Framework for Pose-Constrained Manipulation Planning.' IJRR 2011.

actuator_details: Three-finger underactuated tendon-driven hand. Each finger: two phalanges with passive compliant joints and a single tendon for flexion + a spring antagonist for extension. Whole hand: three motors (one per finger) plus optional palm-rotation degree of freedom. Designed for inherent grasp robustness via underactuation and compliant adaptation. ReFlex SF (Sensorized Finger) variant adds tactile fingertip sensors via the TakkTile MEMS array technology.
control_architecture: Single-DoF-per-finger tendon position or torque control; passive compliance handles object shape variation. Yale OpenHand Project provides multiple parametric hand variants (Model M, Model O, Model T42) all sharing the underactuated-tendon paradigm. Open-source ROS drivers for ReFlex SF.
creator: Lael Odhner, Aaron Dollar, Robert Howe; Yale GRAB Lab and Harvard BioRobotics; with RightHand Robotics, Inc. as the commercial spinout (ReFlex SF/TakkTile)
disclosure_citation: Odhner, Lael U.; Jentoft, Leif P.; Claffee, Mark R.; Corson, Nicholas; Tenzer, Yaroslav; Ma, Raymond R.; Buehler, Martin; Kohout, Robert; Howe, Robert D.; Dollar, Aaron M. 'A compliant, underactuated hand for robust manipulation.' International Journal of Robotics Research, Volume 33, Issue 5, April 2014, pp. 736-752. DOI: 10.1177/0278364913514466. Yale OpenHand Project release: Ma, R. R. and Dollar, A. M. 'Yale OpenHand Project: Optimizing Open-Source Hand Designs for Ease of Fabrication and Adoption.' IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine, Volume 24, Issue 1, March 2017, pp. 32-40. DOI: 10.1109/MRA.2016.2639034. Open-hardware repository at https://www.eng.yale.edu/grablab/openhand/.
end_effector: three-finger underactuated tendon-driven hand with optional palm rotation
ip_citations: Yale OpenHand Project documents are released under permissive open-hardware terms
notable_capabilities: robust grasping without explicit perception via compliant underactuation
TakkTile barometric tactile sensing (ReFlex SF variant)
Yale OpenHand Project provides parametric design family
prior_art_notes: Yale OpenHand / ReFlex SF (Odhner-Dollar et al. IJRR 2014; Yale OpenHand Project IEEE RAM 2017) is the canonical open-hardware academic disclosure of underactuated tendon-driven robust grasping hands. Anticipates with full open-hardware specificity: (1) the three-finger underactuated tendon-driven gripper with passive compliance — directly relevant to claims on simple-grasp humanoid end-effectors; (2) the open-hardware design release pattern (CAD files, BOMs, fabrication instructions) for robotic hands — relevant to claims on 3D-printable robotic hand IP (predates and anticipates many late-2010s and 2020s open-hardware hand patents); (3) the compliant-grasp-without-perception paradigm as an alternative to dexterous-perception-driven manipulation — relevant to claims on perception-light humanoid grasping; (4) integration of barometric tactile sensors (TakkTile) into a robot hand — relevant to claims on humanoid tactile fingertip IP. Yale GRAB Lab has continuous publication record on underactuated hands since the early 2000s; the 2014 IJRR consolidates the design canon. Modern open-hardware humanoid hand IP filings face this 12-year-deep open-source academic anchor.
sensing: joint encoders, motor torque; ReFlex SF adds TakkTile barometric tactile arrays at the fingertips and proximal pads

actuator_details: Algorithmic and control disclosure on the original Boston Dynamics Atlas hydraulic humanoid (DRC-era; 28 hydraulically actuated DoF, ~150 kg). Papers describe whole-body QP-based inverse-dynamics control, footstep-region MIP planning (Deits-Tedrake 2014), iterative SQP trajectory optimization, contact-aware Kalman-filter state estimation, and the IRIS region-of-attraction footstep planner. Publications cover Atlas's entire controller stack as deployed at the DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals (June 2015).
canonical_name: Atlas academic publications (Kuindersma et al., DRC era)
control_architecture: Whole-body inverse-dynamics QP control: at every control step solve a quadratic program for joint torques minimizing tracking error subject to contact constraints, friction cones, and torque limits. Footstep planning via mixed-integer convex optimization over the IRIS regions decomposition of free space. Trajectory optimization via direct transcription with SQP. Contact-aware EKF state estimation. The Kuindersma 2016 AURO paper provides the consolidated end-to-end controller architecture.
creator: Scott Kuindersma, Russ Tedrake, Robin Deits, Maurice Fallon, Andrés Valenzuela, Hongkai Dai, Frank Permenter, Twan Koolen, Pat Marion; MIT CSAIL Robot Locomotion Group (DRC Atlas team)
disclosure_citation: Kuindersma, Scott; Permenter, Frank; Tedrake, Russ. 'An efficiently solvable quadratic program for stabilizing dynamic locomotion.' IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), Hong Kong, June 2014, pp. 2589-2594. DOI: 10.1109/ICRA.2014.6907230. Consolidated Atlas-on-DRC paper: Kuindersma, S.; Deits, R.; Fallon, M.; Valenzuela, A.; Dai, H.; Permenter, F.; Koolen, T.; Marion, P.; Tedrake, R. 'Optimization-based locomotion planning, estimation, and control design for the Atlas humanoid robot.' Autonomous Robots 40(3): 429-455, March 2016. DOI: 10.1007/s10514-015-9479-3.
notable_capabilities: whole-body QP inverse-dynamics control on hydraulic humanoid
mixed-integer footstep planning over IRIS regions
open-source Drake-based simulation code accompanies papers
power_source: tethered (DRC Atlas hydraulic) / battery (later Atlas variants)
prior_art_notes: The MIT DRC Atlas academic publication trail (Kuindersma-Tedrake et al. 2014-2016) is distinct from the Boston Dynamics Atlas product entry (atlas-boston-dynamics) and from the Sentis-Khatib WBOSC entry: it is the canonical academic disclosure of the actually-deployed Atlas controller stack as fielded at the DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals (June 2015). Anticipates with element-by-element specificity: (1) whole-body QP-based inverse-dynamics control on a hydraulically-actuated humanoid platform — directly relevant to commercial claims on QP-based humanoid IP (every modern humanoid runs a derivative); (2) the IRIS-regions mixed-integer convex footstep planner — relevant to claims on footstep-planning humanoid IP; (3) iterative SQP trajectory optimization with contact schedule — anticipates claims overlapping Crocoddyl (mastalli-crocoddyl-2020) and DDP approaches; (4) the consolidated end-to-end stack documentation in AURO 2016 — the most complete public disclosure of a working DRC-class humanoid control architecture. Drake source code accompanies the publications under BSD license. Modern QP-IDC-based humanoid IP filings face this 12-year-deep academic anchor with full implementation disclosure.
sensing: Multisense SL stereo+LiDAR head, joint position, IMU, hydraulic pressure sensors, force-torque at wrists/feet
sources: Kuindersma, S.; Permenter, F.; Tedrake, R. 'An efficiently solvable quadratic program for stabilizing dynamic locomotion.' ICRA 2014: 2589-2594. DOI: 10.1109/ICRA.2014.6907230.
Kuindersma, S. et al. 'Optimization-based locomotion planning, estimation, and control design for the Atlas humanoid robot.' Autonomous Robots 40(3): 429-455, 2016. DOI: 10.1007/s10514-015-9479-3.
Deits, R. and Tedrake, R. 'Footstep planning on uneven terrain with mixed-integer convex optimization.' IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2014.
Drake source code: https://drake.mit.edu, BSD-3-Clause license (companion to the Atlas papers).

actuator_details: Torque-controlled bipedal humanoid based on the DLR LWR-III joint design: brushless DC motors with harmonic-drive primary reducers, integrated torque sensors at every joint. Cycloidal-style high-load joints in the legs.
control_architecture: whole-body torque control via passivity-based controllers; divergent component of motion (DCM) for walking; impedance control for whole-body interaction
creator: Englsberger, Werner, Ott, Henze, Roa, Garofalo, Burger, Beyer, Eiberger, Schmid, Albu-Schäffer; DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics
disclosure_citation: Englsberger, J., Werner, A., Ott, C., Henze, B., Roa, M.A., Garofalo, G., Burger, R., Beyer, A., Eiberger, O., Schmid, K., Albu-Schäffer, A. 'Overview of the torque-controlled humanoid robot TORO'. IEEE-RAS Humanoids, July 2014.
prior_art_notes: TORO is the canonical academic disclosure of full-body torque-controlled bipedal humanoid with DCM (Divergent Component of Motion) walking control. Anticipates: (1) torque-controlled whole-body bipedal walking — directly relevant to claims on whole-body torque-controlled humanoid platforms; (2) DCM walking as an alternative to ZMP — relevant to walking-control IP; (3) impedance-control whole-body interaction with humans — relevant to safe-human-interaction humanoid claims. DLR's Englsberger paper introduced the DCM formulation that subsequent humanoids (HRP-5P, several private platforms) adopted. Publicly funded research with extensive IEEE-proceedings publication.
sensing: per-joint torque sensors; joint position encoders; IMU; force-torque at the feet
sources: Englsberger, J. et al. 'Overview of the torque-controlled humanoid robot TORO'. IEEE Humanoids 2014.

actuator_details: Open educational resource for soft-robotics design + fabrication. **Detailed open instructions** for fabricating elastomeric soft actuators (PneuNets, fiber-reinforced bending actuators), electroadhesion grippers, soft sensors. **Free CAD files, video tutorials, materials sourcing**. CC-BY-NC-SA. The de facto academic open-hardware substrate for soft-robotics teaching and research.
control_architecture: Provides fabrication recipes for actuators that downstream control systems use.
creator: Harvard Biodesign Lab + Harvard Microrobotics Lab; Conor Walsh, Robert Wood, Dónal Holland et al.
disclosure_citation: Holland, D. P., Park, E. J., Polygerinos, P., Bennett, G. J., Walsh, C. J. 'The Soft Robotics Toolkit: Shared Resources for Research and Design'. Soft Robotics Vol. 1 No. 3 2014. Wood + Walsh groups, Harvard Biodesign Lab + Harvard Microrobotics Lab.
prior_art_notes: The Harvard Soft Robotics Toolkit is the canonical open-academic soft-robotics fabrication library (Holland et al. Soft Robotics 1(3) 2014; Wood + Walsh group lineage). 11-year-deep open prior art for: elastomeric soft actuators (PneuNets, fiber-reinforced bending), soft sensors, complete fabrication recipes. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on soft-actuator fabrication or soft-sensor design. Particularly relevant for any future free-humanoid-soft variant.

actuator_details: Anthropomorphic five-fingered hand with 19 internal DOFs but only one motor — actuation by a single tendon routed through a 'first synergy' postural pattern (PCA-derived from human grasping). Compliant joints with elastic returns. Underactuated: most fingers passively conform to grasp shape.
control_architecture: single-DOF tendon position control along the principal grasping synergy; passive compliance handles object shape variation
creator: Catalano, Grioli, Farnioli, Serio, Piazza, Bicchi; Centro 'E. Piaggio', Università di Pisa, and Italian Institute of Technology
disclosure_citation: Catalano, M.G., Grioli, G., Farnioli, E., Serio, A., Piazza, C., Bicchi, A. 'Adaptive synergies for the design and control of the Pisa/IIT SoftHand'. International Journal of Robotics Research 33(5): 768-782, November 3, 2014.
notable_capabilities: 19-DOF hand with single motor via synergistic tendon routing
robust grasp on diverse objects without explicit perception
prior_art_notes: The Pisa-IIT SoftHand is the canonical academic disclosure of synergistic underactuated anthropomorphic hands. Anticipates: (1) the use of human-derived postural synergies (specifically the 'first synergy' from PCA on human grasping kinematics) as the actuation pattern for an anthropomorphic robot hand — directly relevant to modern claims on synergy-driven hand IP; (2) reducing 19 DOFs to a single motor via tendon-coupling — relevant to underactuated humanoid hand patents. Bicchi's group has extensive prior art back to the 1990s on underactuated grasping; the SoftHand 2014 paper is the consolidated reference. Heavily cited; commercial extensions exist (qb robotics).
sensing: motor position; cable tension; optional force sensors

actuator_details: Willow Garage PR2 dual-arm humanoid platform (BRETT in Berkeley lab branding). Each arm 7-DoF compliant; 3-finger gripper. End-to-end CNN policy mapping 240×240 RGB to 7-DoF torques learned via guided policy search (GPS): trajectory-optimization-supervised neural-network distillation.
canonical_name: Levine Guided Policy Search end-to-end manipulation on PR2/BRETT
control_architecture: Guided Policy Search: alternates between (a) trajectory optimization under known dynamics from initial states, producing reference trajectories; and (b) supervised neural-network training to imitate the trajectory-optimizer. Final policy is a convolutional network mapping camera pixels directly to torques. Multi-task generalization across coat-hanger, plastic-bottle, hammer, screw insertion.
creator: Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn, Trevor Darrell, Pieter Abbeel, UC Berkeley
disclosure_citation: Levine, Sergey, Finn, Chelsea, Darrell, Trevor, Abbeel, Pieter. 'End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies.' Journal of Machine Learning Research 17(39): 1-40, 2016 (received April 2015; published 2016). Earlier: Levine, S., Wagener, N., Abbeel, P. 'Learning Contact-Rich Manipulation Skills with Guided Policy Search.' ICRA 2015.
notable_capabilities: pixels-to-torques end-to-end visuomotor policy on real humanoid
prior_art_notes: Levine et al. 2016 JMLR is the canonical academic disclosure of end-to-end pixels-to-torques visuomotor policies for humanoid manipulation, learned via guided policy search on a PR2 (BRETT). Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on end-to-end neural-network policies mapping camera observations directly to humanoid actuator commands — Levine's CNN architecture, training pipeline, and on-robot evaluation are explicitly disclosed; (2) claims on trajectory-optimization-supervised distillation as a sample-efficient alternative to model-free RL on physical humanoids — GPS is the headline contribution; (3) claims on multi-task generalization of a single visuomotor network across contact-rich manipulation tasks (coat-hanger, plastic-bottle, hammer, screw insertion). >3500 citations; JMLR open access; arXiv preprint 2015. The lineage runs directly forward to RT-1, RT-2, OpenVLA, and modern humanoid VLA systems. Modern humanoid end-to-end visuomotor IP filings face this 11-year-deep anchor with full architecture disclosure.
sensing: single RGB camera (no depth), proprioception, force-torque
sources: Levine, S., Finn, C., Darrell, T., Abbeel, P. 'End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies.' JMLR 17(39): 1-40, 2016.
Levine, S., Wagener, N., Abbeel, P. 'Learning Contact-Rich Manipulation Skills with Guided Policy Search.' ICRA 2015.
BRETT video archive, UC Berkeley RAIL Lab, 2015.

actuator_details: Visual SLAM system using ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF) features. Three parallel threads: tracking (per-frame ORB matching to local map), local mapping (keyframe culling and bundle adjustment), loop closing (place recognition via bag-of-words + pose graph optimization). Open-source under GPL-v3.
control_architecture: visual perception substrate for humanoid platforms; provides 6-DOF camera pose + sparse 3D map at ~30 Hz on standard hardware
creator: Raul Mur-Artal, J.M.M. Montiel, Juan D. Tardós; University of Zaragoza
disclosure_citation: Mur-Artal, Raul; Montiel, J.M.M.; Tardós, Juan D. 'ORB-SLAM: a versatile and accurate monocular SLAM system'. IEEE Transactions on Robotics 31(5): 1147-1163, October 2015. Extended: ORB-SLAM2 (RGB-D + stereo, 2017); ORB-SLAM3 (visual-inertial + multi-map, 2021).
prior_art_notes: ORB-SLAM is one of the standard reference visual SLAM systems for humanoid platforms. Anticipates: (1) real-time monocular SLAM as a deployable architecture — relevant to claims on humanoid visual localization; (2) the three-thread tracking + mapping + loop-closing architecture — relevant to multi-thread perception humanoid IP; (3) ORB-feature-based place recognition for loop closure — relevant to scene-recognition humanoid claims. The 2015 T-RO paper plus subsequent ORB-SLAM2 (2017) and ORB-SLAM3 (2021) extensions provide deep prior art coverage; the GitHub release (GPL-v3) makes the architecture defensively-published.

actuator_details: **171 cm tall, 80 kg whole-body humanoid** with 32 DoF (head, torso, arms, legs). **Wheel-leg hybrid feet** — a transformable lower-body that can roll on knees for stability or walk bipedally. The transformable architecture was a strategic choice for DRC tasks (driving the car). All-electric brushless DC actuators with planetary gearheads.
control_architecture: Whole-body QP-based balance control + dedicated task-specific behaviors for each DRC task. Two-stage knee-roll-then-stand transformation. Manual operator-supervised autonomy via radio link (DRC required intermittent comm).
creator: KAIST Humanoid Robot Research Center; Jun-Ho Oh group + Rainbow Robotics
disclosure_citation: KAIST + Rainbow Robotics. 'DRC-HUBO+: A robotic platform for the DARPA Robotics Challenge'. Lim, J., Lee, I., Shim, I., et al. International Journal of Robotics Research / Journal of Field Robotics 2017. Won 1st place at DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals Pomona June 2015 — completing all 8 disaster-response tasks in 44m28s. The follow-on commercial version was Rainbow Robotics' first product (corpus has rainbow-robotics-rb-y1 as the modern commercial successor).
notable_capabilities: DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals 2015 1st place — 8/8 tasks, 44m28s
wheel-leg hybrid transformable feet (knee-rolling vs bipedal)
the canonical Korean academic humanoid milestone

Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on transformable lower-body morphology or DRC-class disaster-response capability set. DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals 2015 Pomona results.
KAIST Humanoid Robot Research Center publications.
IEEE Spectrum coverage 'Korean Team Wins DARPA Robotics Challenge' 2015.

actuator_details: Hovering AUV with anthropomorphic upper body. 8-thruster vectored layout for full-6-DoF station-keeping. Two 7-DoF anthropomorphic arms with underactuated 3-finger hands. All-electric brushless thrusters. Pressure-tolerant electronics in oil-filled compartments + pressure hull for battery and main computer.
control_architecture: Bilateral haptic teleoperation via Sigma.7 master controllers (Force Dimension). Operator in surface-ship control room receives stereo video + haptic force feedback at 1 kHz; commands robot motion at 1 kHz via fiber tether. Khatib group's whole-body operational-space framework (1987+ academic lineage) is the control substrate. Open academic publication.

disclosure_citation: Khatib, O., Yeh, X., Brantner, G., et al. 'Ocean One: A Robotic Avatar for Oceanic Discovery'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine vol. 23 no. 4, 2016. First operational dive (La Lune wreck, Mediterranean, 100 m depth) April 2016.
end_effector: 2× anthropomorphic 7-DoF arms with 3-finger underactuated grippers; force/torque sensors at wrists
notable_capabilities: bilateral haptic teleoperation with force feedback
first dive: La Lune wreck (Louis XIV ship, 100 m depth) Mediterranean April 2016
subsequent ops: Crete archeological surveys, deep-water samples
prior_art_notes: OceanOne is the canonical academic bimanual humanoid AUV. 9-year-deep open academic publication via the Khatib group at Stanford. Establishes element-by-element prior art for: 8-thruster vectored layout for humanoid AUV (exact match to free-humanoid-submersible commitment), bimanual 7-DoF anthropomorphic arms underwater, bilateral haptic teleoperation, F/T-sensor-in-the-loop manipulation, integration with Khatib's operational-space framework. Directly anticipates every architectural element of free-humanoid-submersible's design and any Aquanaut/Nauticus commercial claim on the same. The Khatib lineage extends back through Stanford operational-space papers to 1987 (38 years).

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure. Imitation learning formulated as occupancy-measure matching: a discriminator network (GAN-like) learns to distinguish expert state-action pairs from policy state-action pairs, while the policy is trained via TRPO/PPO with the discriminator's negative log-probability as reward.
control_architecture: GAN-style two-network training: (1) discriminator D(s,a) → [0,1] trained to maximize log D(s,a)_expert + log(1 - D(s,a)_policy); (2) policy π(a|s) trained via policy gradient with reward r(s,a) = -log(1 - D(s,a)). Bypasses inverse-RL's expensive cost-function recovery.
creator: Jonathan Ho and Stefano Ermon, Stanford University
disclosure_citation: Ho, Jonathan and Ermon, Stefano. 'Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning.' arXiv:1606.03476, June 10, 2016. NeurIPS 2016: 4565-4573.
end_effector: generic; demonstrated on MuJoCo continuous-control benchmarks including humanoid walker
notable_capabilities: demonstrated on humanoid walker MuJoCo benchmark
prior_art_notes: GAIL is the foundational academic disclosure of GAN-style adversarial imitation learning, providing a sample-efficient alternative to inverse-RL for policy learning from demonstration. Anticipates: (1) the discriminator-as-reward-source paradigm for imitation — directly relevant to claims on humanoid policies trained via adversarial-loss imitation (a common ingredient in modern legged-robot RL pipelines); (2) the elimination of cost-function recovery as a separate step — relevant to claims on end-to-end imitation pipelines for humanoids; (3) the demonstrated MuJoCo Humanoid benchmark transfer — relevant to humanoid-RL patent claims. Heavily cited (>4000 citations). Open-source reference implementation. Modern humanoid adversarial-imitation-learning patent claims face this 10-year-deep anchor.
sources: Ho, J. and Ermon, S. 'Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning.' NeurIPS 2016; arXiv:1606.03476.
Goodfellow, I. et al. 'Generative Adversarial Nets.' NeurIPS 2014 (foundational GAN paper).

actuator_details: Series-elastic actuators
control_architecture: ALIP, reduced-order models, RL

disclosure_citation: Agility Robotics / Oregon State University Cassie release, 2017.

prior_art_notes: Cassie and the broader Hurst lab work on reduced-order locomotion models is significant prior art for bipedal control claims industry-wide.

actuator_details: **The canonical sim-to-real method**. Trains a policy in simulation while randomizing simulator parameters (lighting, textures, camera positions, friction, mass, joint dynamics) so the policy must learn invariances that generalize to the real world. Demonstrated zero-shot transfer of object-detection and manipulation policies from sim to real. **The architectural anchor for every modern sim-to-real workflow**.
control_architecture: Provides a training-procedure pattern, not a runtime system. Composes with any policy class.
creator: OpenAI + UC Berkeley; Tobin, Fong, Ray, Schneider, Zaremba, Abbeel
disclosure_citation: Tobin, J., Fong, R., Ray, A., Schneider, J., Zaremba, W., Abbeel, P. 'Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World'. arXiv:1703.06907, March 2017. IROS 2017. OpenAI + UC Berkeley.
notable_capabilities: zero-shot sim-to-real demonstrated for object detection + manipulation
the architectural anchor of OpenAI Dactyl (in corpus), ANYmal sim-to-real, every modern RL policy
prior_art_notes: Domain Randomization (Tobin et al. IROS 2017) is the foundational sim-to-real method. 8-year-deep public-domain academic prior art. **Cited by every subsequent sim-to-real paper** including OpenAI Dactyl (2018-2019, in corpus), Hwangbo ANYmal sim-to-real (2019), Berkeley Humanoid (round-11, 2024), Berkeley Humanoid Lite (round-11, 2025), ToddlerBot (round-11, 2025). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on sim-to-real training methodology. The technique is too general to patent — but having it as a corpus entry resolves ~50 prior_art_notes references that previously referred to it informally.
sources: Tobin et al. arXiv:1703.06907 March 2017; IROS 2017.

actuator_details: **Vision-based tactile sensor with 3D-printed biomimetic skin**. An internal camera images the inner surface of an elastomeric fingertip-shaped 3D-printed skin embedded with white-marker papillae (mimicking skin's intermediate-epidermal ridges). When the skin contacts an object, the papillae shift; image-based tracking gives high-resolution tactile signal. Open-hardware design released for free academic use. **The architectural ancestor of Tactile SoftHand-A (round-11) and Educational SoftHand-A (round-12)** — both of which integrate TacTip-class sensors at fingertips.
control_architecture: Provides camera-based tactile-image stream consumable by downstream perception. Open-source.
creator: Bristol Robotics Laboratory; Nathan Lepora group
disclosure_citation: Ward-Cherrier, B., Pestell, N., Cramphorn, L., Winstone, B., Giannaccini, M. E., Rossiter, J., Lepora, N. F. 'The TacTip Family: Soft Optical Tactile Sensors with 3D-Printed Biomimetic Morphologies'. Soft Robotics 5(2) 2018; arXiv:1803.04922. Bristol Robotics Laboratory (Lepora group).
end_effector: vision-based tactile fingertip (mountable on grippers / hands)
notable_capabilities: 3D-printed biomimetic papillae skin (architecturally distinct from DIGIT/GelSight)
the architectural ancestor of Tactile SoftHand-A + Educational SoftHand-A
prior_art_notes: TacTip is the canonical academic vision-based tactile sensor with 3D-printed biomimetic skin (Lepora group Bristol, 2017+). 8-year-deep open-permissive prior art predating Meta DIGIT (round-16, 2020) by 3 years; predates GelSight commercialization by ~6 years. **The architectural ancestor of Tactile SoftHand-A (round-11, 2024) and Educational SoftHand-A (round-12, 2025)** — both Lepora-group successors integrating TacTip at fingertips. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on biomimetic-papillae tactile fingertips. Tesla Optimus Gen 3's 'tactile fingertip sensors' claim faces TacTip + DIGIT + GelSight + ReSkin as three modality-distinct prior-art chains.
sources: Ward-Cherrier et al. Soft Robotics 5(2) 2018; arXiv:1803.04922.

actuator_details: Algorithm: trains a reward model from human preference comparisons (which of two trajectory pairs the human prefers) and then trains a policy via standard RL against the learned reward. Demonstrated on Atari and MuJoCo simulated tasks. Roughly 1000 binary preference comparisons sufficient to learn a competitive reward model.
canonical_name: RLHF (Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences)
control_architecture: policy-learning architecture: human preference data → reward model → policy via PPO/A2C-class RL. Foundational for modern LLM alignment (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) and increasingly for humanoid policy alignment.
creator: Paul Christiano, Jan Leike, Tom Brown, Miljan Martic, Shane Legg, Dario Amodei; OpenAI and DeepMind
disclosure_citation: Christiano, Paul; Leike, Jan; Brown, Tom; Martic, Miljan; Legg, Shane; Amodei, Dario. 'Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences'. NeurIPS 2017, June 12, 2017 (arXiv:1706.03741).
notable_capabilities: binary trajectory comparisons as preference signal
prior_art_notes: Christiano et al. 2017 RLHF is the foundational academic disclosure of preference-based reward learning at scale. Anticipates: (1) human-preference-based reward learning as a deployable policy-tuning architecture — directly relevant to modern claims on aligned-humanoid IP that use preference signals; (2) the architecture of separating reward-model learning from policy learning — relevant to modular alignment-and-policy humanoid claims; (3) binary trajectory preference signals as the supervisory mode — relevant to RLHF-on-humanoid claims (Anthropic's Constitutional AI, OpenAI's InstructGPT all build on this foundation, and the technique is being ported to humanoid policy alignment). The 2017 NeurIPS paper plus open-source code on GitHub provide extensive prior art coverage. Modern humanoid alignment IP all face this 9-year academic anchor.
sources: Christiano, P. et al. 'Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences'. NeurIPS 2017 (arXiv:1706.03741).

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure for goal-conditioned RL. Demonstrated on Fetch and Shadow Hand simulation environments. The HER mechanism: relabel failed trajectories with achieved goals as the desired goals, providing dense reward signal even when the original goal was missed.
control_architecture: Goal-conditioned RL with replay-buffer hindsight: every failed trajectory is augmented by replacing the original goal with the actually-achieved final state and computing reward as if that had been the goal. Combines with any off-policy algorithm (DDPG, DQN, etc.).
creator: OpenAI (Andrychowicz, Wolski, Ray, Schneider, Fong, Welinder, McGrew, Tobin, Abbeel, Zaremba)
disclosure_citation: Andrychowicz, Marcin, Wolski, Filip, Ray, Alex, Schneider, Jonas, Fong, Rachel, Welinder, Peter, McGrew, Bob, Tobin, Josh, Abbeel, Pieter, Zaremba, Wojciech. 'Hindsight Experience Replay.' arXiv:1707.01495, July 5, 2017. NeurIPS 2017.
notable_capabilities: data-efficiency improvement of 10x+ in benchmark tasks
prior_art_notes: HER is the canonical academic disclosure of hindsight relabeling for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning. Anticipates: (1) the use of achieved-goal relabeling to convert sparse-reward trajectories into dense-reward training signal — directly relevant to claims on sample-efficient humanoid policy training (every modern humanoid RL pipeline that uses goal-conditioned policies relies on HER or its descendants); (2) the algorithmic decoupling of off-policy RL from the relabeling step — relevant to architecture-agnostic relabeling claims; (3) the demonstration on dexterous manipulation (Shadow Hand simulation) connecting HER to humanoid-relevant tasks. Heavily cited (>3000 citations); NeurIPS 2017. Code released under MIT license. Modern humanoid policy-training patents face this 9-year-deep 102 anchor on hindsight-relabeling RL.
sources: Andrychowicz, M. et al. 'Hindsight Experience Replay.' NeurIPS 2017; arXiv:1707.01495.
Plappert, M. et al. 'Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning: Challenging Robotics Environments and Request for Research.' arXiv:1802.09464, 2018 (extended HER benchmark).

actuator_details: Reimplementation of ROS atop DDS middleware. Supports real-time constraints, multi-machine cross-network communication, and embedded-class deployment that ROS 1 could not. Lifecycle-managed nodes, native security, deterministic execution. The substrate for modern academic + commercial robotics integration.
control_architecture: DDS-based pub/sub middleware; component lifecycle management; QoS-policy-aware messaging.
creator: Open Robotics; multi-author community
disclosure_citation: Open Robotics. ROS 2 'Ardent Apalone' first stable release December 8, 2017. Architectural redesign of ROS atop DDS (Data Distribution Service) for real-time, multi-vehicle, and embedded use. Apache-2.0.
notable_capabilities: deployed on quadrupeds (ANYmal D, Spot), humanoids, AUVs, drones
prior_art_notes: ROS 2 is the modern academic + commercial robotics middleware (2017+). 8-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: real-time DDS-based robotics middleware, lifecycle-managed component architectures for multi-robot systems, QoS-aware inter-vehicle messaging. All four free-humanoid-family morphologies (platform/wheeled/centaur/submersible) commit to ROS 2 as the integration substrate, shielded by this entry.

actuator_details: **Foundational motion-capture-imitation reinforcement learning** for physics-based character animation. Trains a physics-based RL policy that imitates a specific motion-capture clip plus satisfies a task objective (e.g., walk in target direction). Demonstrates results on humanoid + Atlas + dinosaur + dragon characters across locomotion, acrobatics (flips, spins), martial arts. **The architectural anchor of subsequent imitation-from-demonstration humanoid policies** including AMP, ASE, and the bipedal-RL literature 2018-2024.
control_architecture: PPO-trained policy with imitation reward (matching reference motion) + task reward. Policy outputs joint torques.
creator: UC Berkeley + UBC; Xue Bin (Jason) Peng, Pieter Abbeel, Sergey Levine, Michiel van de Panne
disclosure_citation: Peng, X. B., Abbeel, P., Levine, S., van de Panne, M. 'DeepMimic: Example-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning of Physics-Based Character Skills'. ACM Transactions on Graphics 37(4) 2018 (SIGGRAPH 2018). arXiv:1804.02717. UC Berkeley + UBC.
notable_capabilities: first deep-RL imitation of motion-capture clips for physics-based characters
demonstrated on humanoid + Atlas + non-human characters
complex skills: backflips, spins, cartwheels, kicks
prior_art_notes: DeepMimic (Peng et al. SIGGRAPH 2018) is the canonical foundational motion-capture-imitation deep-RL framework. 7-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: deep-RL imitation of motion-capture references, physics-based character animation via RL, complex acrobatic skill (backflip, spin) RL training. **The architectural ancestor of**: Adversarial Motion Priors (round-21 entry below), ASE (Peng et al. 2022), the entire humanoid-from-mocap-data line. actuator_details: Ghost Robotics Minitaur 8-DOF quadruped (parallel-elastic actuators with quasi-direct-drive). Trained via PPO in PyBullet simulation with system identification + actuator latency modeling + observation noise.

notable_capabilities: active 2-link tail (architectural innovation vs. STAR baseline)

actuator_details: Dynamic-scene visual SLAM built atop ORB-SLAM2. Detects moving objects via multi-view geometry + Mask R-CNN deep learning, then **inpaints the static background** that was occluded by dynamic objects. Produces a static-only map suitable for long-term applications. The canonical foundational dynamic SLAM system.

creator: University of Zaragoza I3A; Bescos, Fácil, Civera, Neira

notable_capabilities: dynamic-object detection via multi-view geometry + Mask R-CNN
background inpainting for static map construction
outperforms ORB-SLAM2 baselines on dynamic TUM-RGBD sequences
the foundational reference for dynamic-scene visual SLAM

actuator_details: Shadow Dexterous Hand (24 DOF) hardware. Visual perception via three RGB cameras + motion capture. Sim-to-real with massively-randomized physics simulation.
control_architecture: reinforcement-learned policy (LSTM-based) trained in simulation with extensive domain randomization across mass, friction, damping, lighting, observation noise, etc. Policy deployed zero-shot to real hand.
creator: Andrychowicz, Akkaya, Mordatch, Plappert, Petron, Powell, Wong, Schneider, Tezak, Tobin, et al.; OpenAI
disclosure_citation: Andrychowicz, M. et al. 'Learning Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation'. arXiv:1808.00177, July 30, 2018; OpenAI. Akkaya, I. et al. 'Solving Rubik's Cube with a Robot Hand'. arXiv:1910.07113, October 16, 2019.
prior_art_notes: Dactyl is the foundational academic disclosure of large-scale sim-to-real RL for in-hand dexterous manipulation. Anticipates: (1) zero-shot policy transfer from massively-randomized simulation to real hardware — directly relevant to claims on sim-to-real humanoid manipulation IP (every modern humanoid hand uses this paradigm); (2) automatic domain randomization (ADR) as a self-tuning training procedure — relevant to claims on adaptive-randomization training; (3) LSTM-based policies for partial-observability manipulation — relevant to recurrent-policy IP. OpenAI's open-source code release plus the arXiv preprints provide deep prior art coverage. Modern in-hand-manipulation claims face this 2018-2019 anchor.

actuator_details: Augmented two-synergy underactuated anthropomorphic hand: 19 internal DoFs driven by TWO motors (vs. one in the original SoftHand). Each motor drives an independent tendon routed through a distinct postural synergy derived from PCA on human grasping kinematics. The two synergies span a richer subspace of grasp+manipulation than the single-synergy predecessor — the second synergy enables abduction/adduction patterns and limited in-hand manipulation. Compliant elastic-return joints throughout; passive shape adaptation.
control_architecture: Two-DoF tendon position control along the two principal grasping synergies; supports in-hand re-grasping by trajectories within the augmented synergy subspace. Compliant joints handle object shape variation passively, eliminating the need for explicit perception-driven grasp planning.
creator: Cosimo Della Santina, Cristina Piazza, Giorgio Grioli, Manuel G. Catalano, Antonio Bicchi; Centro 'E. Piaggio', Università di Pisa, and Italian Institute of Technology (IIT)
disclosure_citation: Della Santina, Cosimo; Piazza, Cristina; Grioli, Giorgio; Catalano, Manuel G.; Bicchi, Antonio. 'Toward Dexterous Manipulation With Augmented Adaptive Synergies: The Pisa/IIT SoftHand 2.' IEEE Transactions on Robotics, Volume 34, Issue 5, October 2018, pp. 1141-1156. DOI: 10.1109/TRO.2018.2830407. First public disclosure as a conference work in earlier 2017 venues; the consolidated T-RO paper is the canonical reference.
notable_capabilities: 19-DoF anthropomorphic hand with only 2 motors via augmented synergies
in-hand manipulation enabled by the second synergy direction
passive shape adaptation via compliant elastic returns
prior_art_notes: Pisa-IIT SoftHand 2 (Della Santina et al. T-RO 2018) is the canonical academic disclosure of multi-synergy augmented underactuated anthropomorphic hands, extending the 2014 SoftHand from one synergy to two. Anticipates with element-by-element specificity: (1) the augmented multi-synergy actuation pattern that enables 19-DoF hand operation with 2 motors and provides in-hand manipulation capability — directly relevant to claims on low-motor-count dexterous humanoid hand IP (Tesla Optimus claimed motor-counts in the 11-22 range, Figure-02 hand counts similar; the SoftHand 2 paradigm anticipates the underactuation-with-manipulation-capability angle of those claims); (2) the formal extension of synergy theory from grasping (one synergy) to grasping-plus-manipulation (two synergies) — relevant to claims on synergy-based humanoid manipulation IP; (3) compliant passive shape adaptation eliminating perception-driven grasp planning — relevant to claims on perception-light humanoid grasping IP. Heavily cited (>200); consolidates Bicchi-group underactuation lineage from the 1990s. Modern multi-synergy underactuated humanoid hand IP filings face this 8-year-deep academic anchor.
sensing: motor positions (2), cable tensions, optional fingertip force sensors
sources: Della Santina, C. et al. 'Toward Dexterous Manipulation With Augmented Adaptive Synergies: The Pisa/IIT SoftHand 2.' IEEE T-RO 34(5): 1141-1156, October 2018. DOI: 10.1109/TRO.2018.2830407.
Catalano, M.G. et al. 'Adaptive synergies for the design and control of the Pisa/IIT SoftHand'. IJRR 33(5), 2014 (predecessor entry pisa-iit-softhand).

Stereo cameras (front and rear), 360° lidar (Velodyne VLP-16), 360° fisheye RGB array, audio array. Built explicitly for human-environment navigation research.

'JRDB: A Dataset and Benchmark for Visual Perception for Navigation in Human Environments.' arXiv:1910.11792, October 2019. It anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on temporal-difference learning, Q-learning, SARSA, and n-step bootstrapping — all derived with closed-form pseudocode in Chapters 6-7; (2) claims on policy-gradient and actor-critic methods — Chapter 13 contains the REINFORCE and natural-actor-critic formulations; (3) claims on function-approximation RL with linear features and neural-network state representations — Chapters 9-12 lay the formal substrate. Freely distributed online by the authors at incompleteideas.net/book under unrestricted educational use. Modern humanoid RL-policy IP claiming any TD/PG/AC pattern faces this canonical 2018 anchor.

actuator_details: Model-based design + verification toolkit for robotics. Multibody dynamics + collision + contact + linear/nonlinear systems theory + MPC + LCP/QP solvers in a unified C++/Python framework. Strong emphasis on formal verification and deterministic semantics — the feature distinguishing Drake from MuJoCo. Used at MIT, TRI, Boston Dynamics, and across academia.
control_architecture: Multibody dynamics + systems framework + optimization-based control toolkit. Provides MPC / TVLQR / QP-based whole-body control templates.
creator: MIT CSAIL Robot Locomotion Group + Toyota Research Institute; Russ Tedrake et al.
disclosure_citation: Tedrake, R., the Drake Development Team. 'Drake: Model-Based Design and Verification for Robotics'. drake.mit.edu, project active since ~2010 with formal v1.0 in January 2019. BSD-3-Clause source: github.com/RobotLocomotion/drake. MIT CSAIL + Toyota Research Institute.
notable_capabilities: Tedrake's MIT 6.832 underactuated robotics course substrate
prior_art_notes: Drake is the canonical MIT/TRI model-based design + verification toolkit for robotics (Tedrake et al., active since ~2010, v1.0 Jan 2019). 6-year-deep formal-release prior art, 15-year-deep project. Distinct from MuJoCo by emphasis on deterministic verifiable semantics (relevant for safety-critical / certification use cases). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on verifiable model-based control or whole-body QP/MPC architectures. Free-humanoid-platform/wheeled/centaur/submersible all reference Drake as a tertiary simulator option for whole-body MPC validation.

zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for legged locomotion
prior_art_notes: Hwangbo et al. 2019 is the foundational academic disclosure of practical RL-based sim-to-real legged locomotion. Published in Science Robotics; one of the most-cited robotics RL papers (>2000 citations). Modern humanoid sim-to-real claims face this 7-year-deep anchor with full peer-review defensibility.

Together they establish the hybrid-locomotion academic substrate.

actuator_details: **Foundational manipulation benchmark** with 100+ unique hand-designed tasks. Built on CoppeliaSim physics with the Franka Panda + Kinova arm setup. Provides expert demonstrations + RL + vision-based observations. The first widely-adopted academic robot-manipulation benchmark and the conceptual ancestor of robomimic, LIBERO, RoboCasa, SimplerEnv.
control_architecture: Provides task suite + observation/action API for IL/RL benchmarking.
creator: Imperial College London Dyson Robotics Lab; Stephen James, Andrew Davison
disclosure_citation: James, S., Ma, Z., Arrojo, D. R., Davison, A. J. 'RLBench: The Robot Learning Benchmark & Learning Environment'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 5(2) 2020. arXiv:1909.12271. Imperial College London Dyson Robotics Lab.
notable_capabilities: expert demos + RL + vision observation modes
RA-L 2020 publication; foundational benchmark cited by ~all subsequent benchmarks
prior_art_notes: RLBench is the foundational academic robot manipulation benchmark (James et al. RA-L 2019). 6-year-deep open-permissive prior art. The conceptual ancestor of robomimic (round-16, 2021), Meta-World (2019), LIBERO (round-17, 2023), RoboCasa (round-16, 2024), SimplerEnv (round-17, 2024). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid manipulation-benchmark claim. Particularly relevant because RLBench tasks have been re-implemented across multiple simulators (CoppeliaSim, MuJoCo, Isaac Gym) — establishing that the task-design itself, not the simulator, is the prior art.
sources: James et al. arXiv:1909.12271 IEEE RA-L 2020.

actuator_details: **Half-humanoid space robot** (head + 2 arms + upper torso; no legs). Skull: 800 g, ~200×220 mm, high-strength aluminum alloy. Female-form anthropomorphic upper body with facial expressions + speech (Hindi + English). Designed for cabin tasks aboard Gaganyaan crewed spacecraft: switch-panel operation, environment-control + life-support system handling, parameter monitoring + telemetry. 2-year planned operational span in orbit.
control_architecture: Cabin-task autonomy + ground-controlled supervision via Gaganyaan downlink. Trade-secret ISRO software stack.

disclosure_citation: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). Vyommitra reveal January 22 2020 at Symposium on Human Spaceflight, Bengaluru. Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala) led design + fabrication. Planned first space flight: Gaganyaan-1 Q4 2025; subsequent Gaganyaan-2 2026. The first Indian humanoid robot for space.
end_effector: 2 anthropomorphic arms (specific DoF + end-effector configuration trade-secret)
notable_capabilities: first Indian humanoid robot for space
designed by Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre / ISRO
prior_art_notes: ISRO Vyommitra is the canonical Indian humanoid space-robot (2020+, Gaganyaan-1 launch Q4 2025). 5-year-deep public-domain prior art for: half-humanoid (no-legs) anthropomorphic upper-body for spacecraft cabin operation, bilingual (Hindi + English) speech-interfaced robot, female-form humanoid for crew-substitute missions. Direct architectural successor to NASA Robonaut 1+2 (corpus entries) for ISS deployment. **The first humanoid-robot entry from India in the corpus** — closes a major regional gap.

actuator_details: PhysX-based articulated-object simulator with the **PartNet-Mobility dataset** of part-level interactable 3D objects. Photorealistic rendering + advanced depth-noise simulation for sim-to-real. The substrate for ManiSkill (manipulation skill framework + benchmark).
control_architecture: Standard sim substrate; ROS control interface; Python API.
creator: UC San Diego + Stanford; Hao Su, Leonidas Guibas, Angel Chang group
disclosure_citation: Xiang, F., Qin, Y., Mo, K., Xia, Y., Zhu, H., Liu, F., Liu, M., Jiang, H., Yuan, Y., Wang, H., Yi, L., Chang, A. X., Guibas, L. J., Su, H. 'SAPIEN: A SimulAted Part-based Interactive ENvironment'. arXiv:2003.08515, March 2020. CVPR 2020. UC San Diego + Stanford. ManiSkill follow-up framework via haosulab/ManiSkill (Hillbot Inc.).
prior_art_notes: SAPIEN is the canonical PartNet-Mobility-based articulated-object simulator (Xiang et al. CVPR 2020). 5-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: part-level mobility annotation in robotic simulation, depth-noise modeling for sim-to-real, ManiSkill manipulation benchmark suite. Distinct from MuJoCo (rigid-body baseline), Isaac Gym (GPU-parallelized), and Genesis (multi-physics) by emphasis on articulated-object interaction. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on articulated-object manipulation training simulation.
sources: Xiang et al. arXiv:2003.08515 March 2020; CVPR 2020.

actuator_details: Software framework, not a physical platform. C++ library with Python bindings for multi-contact optimal control via differential-dynamic-programming-class methods. BSD-3-Clause license. Builds on Pinocchio (Carpentier 2019) for analytical rigid-body dynamics derivatives. Supports floating-base humanoid and quadruped platforms (TALOS, ANYmal, HRP-2, Atlas). Provides DDP, FDDP (feasibility-driven DDP), and BoxDDP (control-limited DDP) solvers.
aliases: Contact RObot COntrol by Differential DYnamic programming Library
control_architecture: Multi-contact differential dynamic programming framework. Models multi-phase contact schedules (left foot, right foot, double support, manipulation contacts) and solves trajectory optimization through them with analytical derivatives via Pinocchio. Used in real-time MPC pipelines on TALOS, ANYmal, and Cassie. The FDDP variant of Mastalli 2020 improves feasibility behavior compared to vanilla DDP.
creator: Carlos Mastalli, Justin Carpentier, Nicolas Mansard, Sethu Vijayakumar et al.; LAAS-CNRS Toulouse, INRIA Paris (Willow team), University of Edinburgh
disclosure_citation: Mastalli, Carlos; Budhiraja, Rohan; Merkt, Wolfgang; Saurel, Guilhem; Hammoud, Bilal; Naveau, Maximilien; Carpentier, Justin; Vijayakumar, Sethu; Mansard, Nicolas. 'Crocoddyl: An Efficient and Versatile Framework for Multi-Contact Optimal Control.' IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), Paris, May 2020, pp. 2536-2542. DOI: 10.1109/ICRA40945.2020.9196673. Source code at https://github.com/loco-3d/crocoddyl. BSD-3-Clause license.
notable_capabilities: real-time DDP for multi-contact humanoid MPC
analytical rigid-body derivatives via Pinocchio integration
demonstrated on TALOS humanoid, ANYmal, Cassie
prior_art_notes: Crocoddyl (Mastalli et al. ICRA 2020) is the canonical academic open-source framework for multi-contact differential-dynamic-programming-based optimal control of humanoid and legged systems. Anticipates with full source-level disclosure: (1) real-time MPC on full-body humanoid models with multiple contacts — directly relevant to commercial claims on whole-body humanoid MPC (Apptronik, Figure 02, Boston Dynamics electric Atlas all employ DDP/iLQR-class controllers downstream of this paradigm); (2) analytical rigid-body dynamics derivatives integrated with trajectory optimization (via Pinocchio, Carpentier 2019) — relevant to claims on differentiable-dynamics humanoid IP; (3) the multi-phase contact-schedule framework that handles humanoid double-support / single-support / manipulation transitions — relevant to claims on phase-aware humanoid MPC; (4) the FDDP feasibility-driven extension that handles infeasible warm-starts — anticipates claims on robust-warm-start humanoid trajectory optimization. BSD-3-Clause source release plus the ICRA 2020 paper (>500 citations by 2026) make this entry a deep prior art anchor for the humanoid MPC patent space.
sensing: agnostic; framework consumes joint state from any sensor pipeline
sources: Mastalli, C. et al. 'Crocoddyl: An Efficient and Versatile Framework for Multi-Contact Optimal Control.' IEEE ICRA 2020: 2536-2542. DOI: 10.1109/ICRA40945.2020.9196673.
Carpentier, J. et al. 'The Pinocchio C++ library — A fast and flexible implementation of rigid body dynamics algorithms and their analytical derivatives.' SII 2019.

actuator_details: **Vision-based tactile fingertip sensor**. Compact (~30×40 mm package). Inside-out camera images a deformable elastomer fingertip surface; image-derived deformation gives high-resolution tactile signal. **Open-hardware design** with full CAD + assembly instructions + Python SDK released. The de facto open-source academic vision-based tactile sensor.
control_architecture: Provides tactile-image stream consumable by downstream perception. Open-source PyTorch wrapper.
creator: Meta AI Research (formerly Facebook AI); Roberto Calandra group
disclosure_citation: Lambeta, M., Chou, P.-W., Tian, S., Yang, B., Maloon, B., Most, V. R., Stroud, D., Santos, R., Byagowi, A., Kammerer, G., Jayaraman, D., Calandra, R. 'DIGIT: A Novel Design for a Low-Cost Compact High-Resolution Tactile Sensor with Application to In-Hand Manipulation'. IEEE RA-L 5(3) 2020. arXiv:2005.14679. Facebook AI Research (now Meta AI).

notable_capabilities: high spatial resolution (full RGB camera image)
the canonical academic open-source vision-based tactile sensor

Tesla Optimus Gen 3's 'tactile fingertip sensors' claim (round-15 entry, see prior_art_notes) faces this prior art directly. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on fingertip tactile sensing — DIGIT's open-hardware design has been widely replicated by academic groups, plus its commercial cousin GelSight (corpus entry `gelsight`) covers the broader vision-based-tactile chain.

actuator_details: Compact low-cost vision-based tactile sensor based on GelSight principles. RGB camera + RGB LED multi-color illumination + replaceable silicone gel. Designed for integration into commodity robot fingers; <$15 BOM; open-source CAD and software.
control_architecture: image-based deformation reconstruction (similar to GelSight); software stack open-sourced for in-hand manipulation pipelines
creator: Lambeta, Chou, Tian, Yang, Maloon, Most, Stroud, Santos, Byagowi, Kammerer, Jayaraman, Calandra; Facebook AI Research (now Meta AI)

Anticipates: (1) low-cost open-source vision-tactile fingertip — directly relevant to claims on commercial humanoid hand patents that incorporate vision-tactile sensing; (2) form-factor integration of vision-tactile sensors into commodity robot hands — relevant to integrated humanoid hand IP. DIGIT's open-source release (CAD, firmware, software stack on GitHub) creates substantial prior art coverage of integration patterns. Heavily cited in subsequent dexterous-manipulation work.

actuator_details: Architecture: jointly trains an image encoder and a text encoder to embed images and text descriptions into a shared vector space using contrastive loss over 400M (image, text) pairs scraped from the web. Resulting embeddings enable zero-shot classification, image retrieval, image-text alignment for downstream tasks.
control_architecture: visual-language alignment substrate; CLIP embeddings are used as a frozen perception backbone in many VLA humanoid policies (PaLM-E, Open X-Embodiment, RT-2 all use CLIP-class encoders or directly fine-tuned CLIP)
creator: Alec Radford, Jong Wook Kim, Chris Hallacy, Aditya Ramesh, et al.; OpenAI
disclosure_citation: Radford, Alec; Kim, Jong Wook; Hallacy, Chris; Ramesh, Aditya; Goh, Gabriel; Agarwal, Sandhini; Sastry, Girish; Askell, Amanda; Mishkin, Pamela; Clark, Jack; Krueger, Gretchen; Sutskever, Ilya. 'Learning transferable visual models from natural language supervision'. arXiv:2103.00020, February 26, 2021. Published ICML 2021.
prior_art_notes: CLIP 2021 is the foundational academic disclosure of contrastive vision-language pretraining at internet scale. Anticipates: (1) the use of contrastive image-text pretraining as a frozen perception backbone for humanoid VLA policies — directly relevant to modern VLA humanoid claims (RT-2, Open X-Embodiment, OpenVLA, PaLM-E, π-zero all build on CLIP-class architectures); (2) zero-shot perception via natural-language descriptions of target objects — relevant to claims on language-conditioned humanoid manipulation; (3) the architecture of training visual encoders on uncurated web data — relevant to data-scaling claims. Modern VLA humanoid IP all face this 5-year academic anchor.
sources: Radford, A. et al. 'Learning transferable visual models from natural language supervision'. arXiv:2103.00020, ICML 2021.

actuator_details: Visual-inertial SLAM library. ORB feature extraction + bag-of-words place recognition + bundle adjustment over keyframes. Supports monocular, stereo, RGB-D, and visual-inertial sensor configurations. Multi-map operation with map-merging. Real-time on commodity CPU.
control_architecture: Provides SLAM substrate for any robotic platform with a camera. C++ library; ROS 1/2 integration.

disclosure_citation: Campos, C., Elvira, R., Rodríguez, J. J. G., Montiel, J. M. M., Tardós, J. D. 'ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial, and Multimap SLAM'. IEEE Transactions on Robotics 37(6) December 2021, pp. 1874-1890. arXiv:2007.11898. GPLv3 source: github.com/UZ-SLAMLab/ORB_SLAM3. University of Zaragoza.
notable_capabilities: the canonical visual-inertial SLAM baseline since 2021
deployed in countless academic + commercial robotic systems
prior_art_notes: ORB-SLAM3 is the canonical academic visual-inertial SLAM library and 5-year-deep open-source baseline. Heavily-cited (>3000 citations). Anticipates: (1) monocular/stereo/RGB-D + IMU fusion in a unified factor-graph framework, (2) multi-map operation across sessions for long-term autonomy, (3) bag-of-words place recognition for loop closure. Establishes the geometric-only SLAM baseline that semantic/open-vocab SLAM systems (including RADIO-ViPE, round-10 entry) extend. Any humanoid platform claim on visual-inertial SLAM faces this lineage.

actuator_details: **Adversarial Motion Priors (AMP)** — combines DeepMimic-style motion-capture imitation with **GAN-style discriminator** trained to distinguish reference-motion-style from policy-generated motion. Replaces DeepMimic's clip-by-clip imitation with **latent-space style imitation** — the policy can produce task-specific motion that 'looks like' the reference style without exactly tracking any specific clip. Major architectural advance over DeepMimic: **distillation of motion style from unstructured motion-capture corpus** rather than clip-specific imitation.
control_architecture: GAN discriminator distilled from motion-capture corpus + task reward + RL policy. Latent style space.
creator: UC Berkeley; Xue Bin (Jason) Peng, Ze Ma, Pieter Abbeel, Sergey Levine, Angjoo Kanazawa
disclosure_citation: Peng, X. B., Ma, Z., Abbeel, P., Levine, S., Kanazawa, A. 'AMP: Adversarial Motion Priors for Stylized Physics-Based Character Control'. ACM Transactions on Graphics 40(4) 2021 (SIGGRAPH 2021). arXiv:2104.02180. UC Berkeley.
notable_capabilities: GAN-style motion-prior distillation from unstructured mocap corpus
the architectural anchor of subsequent AMP-derived humanoid RL papers
open-source via NVIDIA Isaac Gym + Berkeley repos
prior_art_notes: Adversarial Motion Priors (Peng et al. SIGGRAPH 2021) is the canonical extension of DeepMimic to GAN-style latent-space motion imitation. 4-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: GAN-distilled motion priors, latent-space mocap style imitation, task-conditioned style-aware humanoid RL. **The architectural ancestor of contemporary humanoid-from-mocap RL** including ASE (Peng et al. 2022), HumanPlus (Stanford 2024), ExBody (Stanford 2024), H1 / G1 humanoid policies (Unitree). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on 'humanoid moves like a human' style-aware locomotion.
sources: Peng, X. B. et al. ACM TOG 40(4) 2021; arXiv:2104.02180.

actuator_details: Successor to FSTAR adding **wall-climbing via thrust reversal**. Propellers can produce reversed thrust; combined with 4-wheel drive, the robot drives over steep slopes including walls. Penetrates 25 cm diameter pipes. Ground speed up to 4.5 m/s. The most architecturally extreme STAR-family member to date.
control_architecture: Mode-switching: ground / wall-climbing / pipe-traversal / flight, with shared actuator pool.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; David Zarrouk group
disclosure_citation: Zarrouk, D., et al. 'FCSTAR: Design and Analysis of a Hybrid Flying and Climbing Sprawl-Tuned Robot'. ResearchGate publication 353205537, July 2021. Ben-Gurion University. Builds on FSTAR with thrust-reversal wall-climbing capability.
notable_capabilities: STAR-family extension that further validates shared-actuator-pool design
notes: DRAFT: exact peer-reviewed venue should be verified before promotion to commons-grade.
prior_art_notes: FCSTAR (Ben-Gurion Zarrouk lab, ~2021) is the most architecturally ambitious STAR-family member: 4 modes (ground, wall-climb, pipe, flight) on a single actuator pool. 4-year-deep open-academic prior art for: thrust-reversal wall-climbing, multi-mode-on-shared-actuator-pool reconfiguration, narrow-pipe traversal. Closes the STAR family lineage chain that begins at star-fearing-2013 and ends with dstar-zarrouk-2026 (decoupled FBEM, Jan 2026). The full 13-year-deep STAR family chain: STAR (Berkeley 2013) → RSTAR (Zarrouk 2019) → TSTAR → FSTAR → FCSTAR → AmphiSTAR → DSTAR.

actuator_details: GPU-parallelized physics simulator for robotic RL. End-to-end GPU pipeline: simulation, observation extraction, neural network inference, policy update — no CPU round-trip. Enables thousands of parallel environment instances on a single GPU. The substrate for ANYmal sim-to-real perceptive locomotion (Hwangbo 2019 → Lee 2020 → Miki 2022 lineage).
control_architecture: GPU-batched physics + RL training pipeline. PyTorch / JAX integration.

disclosure_citation: Makoviychuk, V., Wawrzyniak, L., Guo, Y., Lu, M., Storey, K., Macklin, M., Hoeller, D., Rudin, N., Allshire, A., Handa, A., State, G. 'Isaac Gym: High-Performance GPU-Based Physics Simulation For Robot Learning'. NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks. arXiv:2108.10470.
