disclosure_citation: Jiang, H., Xu, Y., Li, K., Feng, J., Zhang, L. 'RoDyn-SLAM: Robust Dynamic Dense RGB-D SLAM with Neural Radiance Fields'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 2024. arXiv:2407.01303 July 2024. Fudan University ZVG (Zhang Vision Group).
notable_capabilities: robust to moving objects in indoor scenes
prior_art_notes: RoDyn-SLAM is Fudan ZVG's NeRF-based dynamic-scene SLAM (IEEE RAL 2024). 10-month-deep prior art on the NeRF branch of dynamic SLAM (distinct from the GS-based lineage of WildGS-SLAM, DGS-SLAM, DG-SLAM, etc.). Cited as a competitor in RADIO-ViPE Table II — the TUM-RGBD ATE benchmark RADIO-ViPE compares against. Together with DGS-SLAM, DG-SLAM, WildGS-SLAM, and DynaSLAM, establishes the academic dynamic-SLAM substrate that RADIO-ViPE measures itself against.
sources: Jiang et al. IEEE RAL 2024; arXiv:2407.01303 July 2024.

actuator_details: Open-source humanoid-teleoperation system using **Apple Vision Pro** as the operator interface. Stereo video from the robot's head streams to the headset (immersive first-person POV); the operator's head + arm + hand pose is mirrored to the robot. Active head tracking (camera twist/tilt) follows operator gaze. Demonstrated on Unitree H1 (with multi-finger hand) and Fourier GR1 (with grippers).
control_architecture: Vision Pro hand+head+gaze tracking → robot teleop. ROS 2 integration. Open-source.
creator: UC San Diego + MIT; Xuxin Cheng, Jialong Li, Shiqi Yang, Ge Yang, Xiaolong Wang
disclosure_citation: Cheng, X., Li, J., Yang, S., Yang, G., Wang, X. 'Open-TeleVision: Teleoperation with Immersive Active Visual Feedback'. arXiv:2407.01512, July 2024. CoRL 2024. UC San Diego + MIT.
notable_capabilities: Apple Vision Pro as operator interface (canonical 2024 first-deployment)
demonstrated on Unitree H1 + Fourier GR1
prior_art_notes: Open-TeleVision is the canonical first open-source academic Apple-Vision-Pro humanoid teleoperation system (Cheng et al. CoRL 2024). 10-month-deep open-permissive prior art for: VR-headset humanoid teleop with first-person stereo POV, active head tracking for gaze-following, hand-pose mirroring across Vision Pro + humanoid arm. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on Apple-Vision-Pro-or-equivalent VR teleop. Architectural successor to Vicarious Surgical (round-16 entry) VR-teleop in surgical context — Open-TeleVision applies the same pattern to humanoid manipulation. The 500-hour Helix (round-15) teleop dataset was likely collected via similar VR-headset teleop infrastructure.
sensing: stereo camera (robot side); Apple Vision Pro hand+head tracking (operator side)

actuator_details: Language-embedded Gaussian-splatting representation built incrementally by a mobile robot. Each Gaussian primitive carries a CLIP-aligned language feature enabling open-vocabulary scene queries. 3.5× faster training than LERF baseline. Demonstrated on a mobile manipulator (Stretch) building room-scale scene representations.
control_architecture: Provides language-grounded scene representation for downstream task-conditioned mobile manipulation.
creator: UC Berkeley AUTOLab; Goldberg group
disclosure_citation: Yu, J., et al. 'LEGS: Language-Embedded Gaussian Splats — Incrementally Building Room-Scale Representations with a Mobile Robot'. IROS 2024. arXiv:2409.18108. UC Berkeley AUTOLab.
end_effector: none (software framework, deployed on Stretch mobile manipulator)
notable_capabilities: open-vocabulary scene queries via CLIP-aligned Gaussian features
incremental room-scale construction by mobile robot
prior_art_notes: LEGS is the canonical Berkeley AUTOLab open-vocabulary Gaussian-splatting representation (IROS 2024). 1.5-year-deep prior art for: CLIP-aligned per-primitive features in 3DGS, incremental room-scale construction by mobile robot, language-grounded mobile-manipulation scene representations. Predates and informs LEG-SLAM, LEGO-SLAM, and any commercial humanoid claim on language-queryable 3D scene maps built onboard.

actuator_details: Vision-language-action **flow model** for general robot control. Pretrained on diverse multi-robot demonstration data (mobile manipulation, bimanual, single-arm). Single foundation policy controls multiple robot embodiments. Action distribution modeled via flow matching (vs. diffusion or autoregressive). Significant step in unified-VLA-foundation-model lineage post RT-2 / OpenVLA.
control_architecture: Foundation-model policy: pretrained VLA + flow-matching action head + per-embodiment fine-tuning.
creator: Physical Intelligence; Black, Brown, Driess, Finn et al.
disclosure_citation: Black, K., Brown, N., Driess, D., Esmail, A., Equi, M., Finn, C., et al. 'π₀: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control'. arXiv:2410.24164, October 2024. Physical Intelligence (physicalintelligence.company).
end_effector: any (policy outputs end-effector commands for the target embodiment)
notable_capabilities: open weights / open paper from Physical Intelligence
prior_art_notes: π₀ is Physical Intelligence's canonical first VLA foundation policy (Oct 2024). 1.5-year-deep open-academic publication. Establishes architectural prior art for: flow-matching action distribution in VLA, cross-embodiment policy pretraining, single foundation model controlling multiple robot platforms. Direct successor lineage from RT-1 (2022), RT-2 (2023), OpenVLA (2024). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on VLA-based control (Tesla Optimus, Figure, 1X NEO, Apptronik all face this); particularly for any claim on flow-matching action heads or cross-embodiment pretraining.

actuator_details: 1.2-billion-parameter diffusion-based VLA foundation model for **bimanual manipulation**. Pre-trained on the largest multi-robot demonstration corpus to date and fine-tuned on a 6K+ episode bimanual dataset. Uses diffusion model formulation (vs. flow-matching π₀ or autoregressive RT-2/OpenVLA) for action distribution.
control_architecture: Diffusion VLA foundation policy. Open-weight via HuggingFace robotics-diffusion-transformer/rdt-1b. Apache-2.0 / similar open license.
creator: Tsinghua TSAIL (THU-ML); Songming Liu et al.
disclosure_citation: Liu, S., et al. 'RDT-1B: a Diffusion Foundation Model for Bimanual Manipulation'. arXiv:2410.07864, October 2024. ICLR 2025. Tsinghua TSAIL (THU-ML) lab.
notable_capabilities: 1.2B parameters — largest diffusion-based robot foundation model
zero-shot generalization to unseen objects + scenes
prior_art_notes: RDT-1B is THU-ML's canonical diffusion-based VLA foundation model for bimanual manipulation (ICLR 2025). 7-month-deep open-permissive prior art for: diffusion-formulation VLA at billion-parameter scale, bimanual manipulation foundation policy, multi-robot pre-training corpus. The canonical Chinese-academy entry in the open-weight VLA race alongside Stanford OpenVLA and Physical Intelligence π₀. Directly cited as a comparison baseline in OpenVLA-OFT (round-12); now resolves correctly. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on diffusion-based bimanual VLA.

control_architecture: GS-SLAM substrate with dynamic-object handling.

disclosure_citation: Kong, M., Lee, J., Lee, S., Kim, E. 'DGS-SLAM: Gaussian Splatting SLAM in Dynamic Environment'. arXiv:2411.10722, November 2024.

actuator_details: **Omnidirectional vision-based tactile sensor in finger form factor**. ~18 cameras inside a hollow cylindrical fingertip image the entire 360° elastomeric surface (vs. DIGIT's flat surface). Anthropomorphic fingertip dimensions. Open-hardware design; CAD + assembly + Python SDK released. Direct successor to DIGIT (round-16) addressing the flat-surface limitation.
control_architecture: Multi-camera tactile-image stream consumable by downstream perception. Open-source.
creator: Meta AI Research / Reality Labs; Calandra group successor team
disclosure_citation: Meta AI / Meta Reality Labs. DIGIT 360 reveal November 2024 via ai.meta.com / digit.ml. Successor to DIGIT (Lambeta + Calandra RA-L 2020, corpus entry `meta-digit-tactile-2020`). Adds omnidirectional 360° finger-shaped tactile sensing surface.

prior_art_notes: DIGIT 360 (Meta, November 2024) is the canonical first omnidirectional vision-based tactile finger. ~6-month-deep open-permissive prior art for: 360° tactile sensing in anthropomorphic finger form factor, multi-camera (18-cam) internal imaging architecture. Direct successor to DIGIT (round-16) closing the flat-surface limitation. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on omnidirectional fingertip tactile sensing — particularly relevant for Tesla Optimus Gen 3 and Figure Helix tactile-claim shielding.

actuator_details: Camera tracking + depth estimation pipeline for in-the-wild monocular videos with dynamic content. Differentiable bundle adjustment layer iteratively updates scene geometry + camera parameters. Integrates monocular depth priors into training and inference. Uncertainty-aware global BA. The closest predecessor to NVIDIA ViPE — RADIO-ViPE / ViPE explicitly cite MegaSaM as the prior baseline.
control_architecture: Provides camera-pose + depth substrate for downstream applications.
creator: Google DeepMind + UC Berkeley + U. Michigan (per arXiv 2412.04463)
disclosure_citation: Authors per arXiv 2412.04463. 'MegaSaM: Accurate, Fast, and Robust Structure and Motion from Casual Dynamic Videos'. arXiv:2412.04463, December 2024. Google DeepMind + UC Berkeley + University of Michigan.
notable_capabilities: robust to dynamic content in casual videos
the closest predecessor to NVIDIA ViPE
notes: DRAFT: full author list should be verified before promotion to commons-grade.
prior_art_notes: MegaSaM (Dec 2024) is the immediate predecessor to NVIDIA ViPE in the calibration-free dynamic-monocular-video pose+depth lineage. 5-month-deep prior art for: differentiable BA with monocular depth priors + uncertainty-aware global BA on in-the-wild dynamic videos. ViPE explicitly outperforms MegaSaM in its results table; that comparison only exists if MegaSaM is the prior art baseline. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on calibration-free in-the-wild video perception.

Multiple variants: Cosmos-Predict (video generation), Cosmos-Transfer (sim-to-real), Cosmos-Reason (video understanding for reasoning). Open weights with permissive commercial license. Used as the foundation for downstream humanoid VLAs (GR00T N1.7 uses Cosmos-Reason2-2B).
control_architecture: Provides world-modeling + reasoning substrate for downstream physical-AI policies.
creator: NVIDIA; multi-author research team
disclosure_citation: NVIDIA. 'Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI'. arXiv:2501.03575, January 2025. NVIDIA CES 2025 announcement. Open weights via HuggingFace nvidia/Cosmos-* family. Cosmos-Reason2-2B variant subsequently used as the System 2 backbone in GR00T N1.7.
notable_capabilities: world foundation models for physical AI
Cosmos-Reason2-2B is the System 2 backbone of GR00T N1.7
prior_art_notes: NVIDIA Cosmos is the canonical world-foundation-model platform for physical AI (NVIDIA CES January 2025). 4-month-deep open-permissive prior art for: video generation + understanding + sim-to-real-transfer foundation models, world-modeling for physical-AI policy training. **Cosmos-Reason2-2B is the System-2 backbone of GR00T N1.7** (round-15 entry); round-17 now resolves that lineage citation. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on world-model-based policy training or on video-generation-based simulation augmentation.

Total BOM under $6,000. Plug-and-play zero-point calibration and transferable motor system identification for sim-to-real.
control_architecture: Designed as ML-compatible substrate. High-fidelity digital twin via system-ID; demonstrated zero-shot sim-to-real policy transfer for both locomotion and manipulation. Loco-manipulation tasks in the demonstration set.
creator: Stanford Robotics Lab; Haochen Shi, Weizhuo Wang, Shuran Song, C. Karen Liu
disclosure_citation: Shi, H., Wang, W., Song, S., Liu, C. K. 'ToddlerBot: Open-Source ML-Compatible Humanoid Platform for Loco-Manipulation'. arXiv:2502.00893, February 2025. Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2025 oral. Stanford Robotics Lab.
notable_capabilities: zero-shot sim-to-real for both loco and manipulation
prior_art_notes: ToddlerBot is Stanford's canonical sub-$6k open-hardware ML-compatible humanoid (CoRL 2025 oral). Establishes 1-year-deep open-academic prior art for: integrated loco-manipulation policy training on an open humanoid platform, transferable motor system-ID for sim-to-real without hand-tuning, 30-DoF anthropomorphic full-body at sub-$6k. Direct shielding for any commercial claim on integrated full-body humanoid policy training, particularly any 'one policy controls the whole body' claim. Together with Berkeley Humanoid Lite, establishes the open-academic baseline for sub-$10k humanoid robotics.
sensing: onboard IMU, joint encoders, RGB camera

actuator_details: Optimized fine-tuning recipe for VLA models, applied to OpenVLA as base. Combines: (1) parallel decoding of action tokens, (2) action chunking, (3) continuous action representation (vs. discretized), (4) L1 regression-based learning objective. Improves OpenVLA average success on LIBERO from 76.5% → 97.1% and increases action throughput by 26×. Real-world bimanual ALOHA evaluations beat π₀ and RDT-1B fine-tuned defaults plus from-scratch Diffusion Policy and ACT by up to 15% absolute success rate.
control_architecture: Fine-tuning recipe for VLA foundation models. Publishes the speed × success Pareto improvement.
creator: Stanford; Moo Jin Kim, Chelsea Finn, Percy Liang
disclosure_citation: Kim, M. J., Finn, C., Liang, P. 'Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models: Optimizing Speed and Success'. arXiv:2502.19645, February 2025. Stanford.
notable_capabilities: 97.1% success on LIBERO (SOTA, vs. OpenVLA 76.5% baseline)
outperforms π₀ + RDT-1B + Diffusion Policy + ACT on bimanual ALOHA
prior_art_notes: OpenVLA-OFT is the canonical Optimized Fine-Tuning recipe for VLA models (Stanford, Feb 2025). 15-month-deep prior art on: parallel action decoding for VLA, action chunking + continuous action representation + L1 regression objective combination. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid VLA fine-tuning claim, particularly any claim on 'fast inference at high success' for humanoid VLAs. Outperforms π₀ on bimanual ALOHA — the canonical academic benchmark for bimanual humanoid manipulation.

actuator_details: Multimodal agent foundation model serving **both digital (UI navigation) and physical (robot manipulation) tasks** under one model. Two distinguishing techniques: **Set-of-Mark (SoM)** — annotated key objects/UI elements relevant to a goal; **Trace-of-Mark (ToM)** — extends SoM to dynamic videos by overlaying tracing lines following object motion through interaction. Magma-8B variant has open weights via HuggingFace.
control_architecture: Multimodal foundation policy unified across digital and physical action spaces. SoM + ToM as visual-grounding annotations.
creator: Microsoft Research; Jianwei Yang et al.
disclosure_citation: Yang, J., et al. 'Magma: A Foundation Model for Multimodal AI Agents'. arXiv:2502.13130, February 2025. CVPR 2025. Microsoft Research.
end_effector: any (cross-domain: digital UI agents + physical manipulators)
notable_capabilities: unified digital + physical agent foundation model
SOTA on UI navigation + robot manipulation simultaneously
prior_art_notes: Magma is Microsoft's canonical multimodal agent foundation model (CVPR 2025). 3-month-deep prior art for: unified digital + physical task foundation policy, Set-of-Mark + Trace-of-Mark visual grounding annotations. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on 'one model controls both robot manipulation AND computer/phone interaction' (a notable claim cluster from 1X NEO marketing and Sanctuary Phoenix demos). Magma-8B's open weights make it a re-implementable baseline that any commercial claim must outperform on UI + robot benchmarks to differentiate.

actuator_details: Real-time whole-body model-predictive controller using MuJoCo dynamics directly. Iterative LQR (iLQR) optimization with finite-difference approximation of dynamics derivatives — no analytical model required. Achieves real-time on hardware for: dynamic quadruped locomotion, quadruped walking on two legs, and full-sized humanoid bipedal locomotion.
control_architecture: Whole-body MPC substrate via MuJoCo. Open-source release on github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco_mpc.
creator: Google DeepMind; Howell, Lutter, Tassa et al.
disclosure_citation: Howell, T., Lutter, M., Acero, F., Yuan, M., Tassa, Y., et al. 'Whole-Body Model-Predictive Control of Legged Robots with MuJoCo'. arXiv:2503.04613, March 2025. Google DeepMind / Tassa group.
notable_capabilities: real-time whole-body MPC at humanoid scale
demonstrated on quadruped and full-sized humanoid hardware
direct extension of the Tassa iLQG (2012) lineage
prior_art_notes: Howell-Tassa MuJoCo MPC is the direct 2025 successor to the Tassa iLQG 2012 entry already in the corpus. 14-month-deep open-permissive prior art for: real-time whole-body humanoid MPC using MuJoCo dynamics + finite-difference iLQR. Demonstrated on full-sized humanoid hardware, which closes the simulation-to-real gap that the 2012 Tassa work left open. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on real-time whole-body trajectory optimization.

actuator_details: **Vision-Language-Action foundation model purpose-built for humanoid robots.** Dual-system architecture inspired by human cognition: System 1 fast-thinking action model (reflex-class); System 2 slow-thinking deliberate-decision model. 2B parameters in the public N1 release. Trained on a diverse mix: **egocentric human videos + real robot trajectories + simulated robot trajectories + synthetic data**. The N1.7 successor adds Cosmos-Reason2-2B VLM backbone + 20,854-hour EgoScale pre-training across 20+ task categories.
control_architecture: Dual-system VLA: S2 internet-pretrained reasoning model + S1 fast reactive policy. Direct architectural lineage with Figure Helix's S1/S2 design (round-15 entry below). Generalizes across grasping, moving objects with one or both arms, and multi-step long-context tasks.
creator: NVIDIA; multi-author research team
disclosure_citation: NVIDIA. 'GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots'. arXiv:2503.14734, March 2025. NVIDIA GTC 2025 announcement. Open commercial license; open weights via HuggingFace nvidia/GR00T-N1-2B. Successor versions N1.6 (full-body) and N1.7 (Cosmos-Reason2 + EgoScale 20K-hour egocentric pre-training) released subsequently.
end_effector: any humanoid (designed for the humanoid form factor specifically)
notable_capabilities: first open commercial-licensed humanoid foundation model
trained on egocentric human video + sim + real
prior_art_notes: NVIDIA GR00T N1 is the canonical first open commercial-licensed humanoid foundation model (GTC March 2025). 2-month-deep open prior art for: dual-system S1/S2 humanoid VLA, egocentric-human-video pre-training at scale, NVIDIA Isaac platform integration. Direct architectural sibling of Figure Helix (round-15 entry). Both adopt the dual-system pattern from cognitive science. The N1.7 EgoScale 20K-hour pre-training corpus is itself prior art for any commercial humanoid claim on egocentric-video-trained policy datasets. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid VLA claim.

actuator_details: Sub-$5,000 open-source 3D-printed humanoid. ~0.8 m tall, ~16 kg. **3D-printed cycloidal-gear actuators** — the design choice that makes the BOM accessible — paired with widely-available off-the-shelf brushless motors. Modular gearbox replaceable per finger / joint. The design explicitly trades absolute durability for reproducibility and democratization.
control_architecture: RL-trained locomotion controller; zero-shot sim-to-real demonstrated. Hardware design + embedded code + training/deployment frameworks all fully open-source. Designed for researchers, students, and tech newbies — explicitly democratization-oriented.
creator: UC Berkeley Hybrid Robotics Lab; Sreenath group
disclosure_citation: Cui, F., Sayle, J., Karydis, K., Liao, Q., et al. 'Demonstrating Berkeley Humanoid Lite: An Open-source, Accessible, and Customizable 3D-printed Humanoid Robot'. arXiv:2504.17249, April 2025. Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2025. UC Berkeley Hybrid Robotics Lab.
notable_capabilities: complete open-source release: hardware CAD + firmware + training
prior_art_notes: Berkeley Humanoid Lite is the canonical sub-$5k open-hardware academic bipedal humanoid (RSS 2025). 1-year-deep prior art on: 3D-printed cycloidal reducer humanoid actuator (a specific architectural commitment), full open-source release of hardware + firmware + training, sub-$5k humanoid BOM, RL-controlled walking on a 3D-printed platform. **Direct shielding for free-humanoid-platform** — particularly the 3D-printed actuator path and any commercial claim on accessible humanoid hardware. Together with ToddlerBot and Berkeley Humanoid (full-size), establishes a deep open-academic substrate for any commercial humanoid platform claim.

actuator_details: Monocular Gaussian-splatting SLAM specifically engineered for dynamic-scene robustness. Tracks camera trajectory and reconstructs a 3D Gaussian map of the static environment from monocular video, even with dynamic distractors (people, moving objects). Renders high-fidelity novel views of the static scene from the trained Gaussian field.
control_architecture: Provides SLAM substrate. Open-source release.
creator: Jianhao Zheng, Zihan Zhu, Valentin Bieri, Marc Pollefeys (ETH Zürich), Songyou Peng, Iro Armeni (Stanford GradientSpaces)
disclosure_citation: Zheng, J., Zhu, Z., Bieri, V., Pollefeys, M., Peng, S., Armeni, I. 'WildGS-SLAM: Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM in Dynamic Environments'. CVPR 2025. arXiv:2504.03886. ETH Zürich + Stanford GradientSpaces.
notable_capabilities: dynamic-scene robust (people + moving objects do not corrupt map)
Gaussian-splatting reconstruction with photorealistic novel views
prior_art_notes: WildGS-SLAM is the canonical CVPR 2025 monocular dynamic-scene Gaussian-splatting SLAM system from ETH + Stanford. Establishes 1-year-deep prior art for: monocular GS-SLAM with dynamic-scene robustness, photorealistic novel-view rendering of static background while filtering dynamic foreground. Among the systems RADIO-ViPE benchmarks against (TUM-RGBD dynamic). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on monocular dynamic-scene mapping with photorealistic reconstruction.

actuator_details: VLA model with **open-world generalization**. Co-trains on heterogeneous tasks: data from multiple robots, high-level semantic subtask prediction, web data, and other sources. Hybrid multi-modal examples combine image observations + language commands + object detections + semantic-subtask prediction + low-level actions. Demonstrates long-horizon (10-15 minute) dexterous manipulation in **entirely new homes** not present in training data — first VLA to convincingly demonstrate this.
control_architecture: Co-trained VLA foundation policy with mixed-modality training data; fine-tuned per-task or zero-shot to new homes for mobile manipulation.
creator: Physical Intelligence; Black et al.
disclosure_citation: Black, K., et al. 'π₀.₅: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization'. arXiv:2504.16054, April 2025. CoRL 2025 (PMLR vol. 305 pp. 17-40, Black25a). Physical Intelligence.
notable_capabilities: long-horizon dexterous tasks (10-15 minutes, kitchen/bedroom cleaning)
co-training on multi-robot + web + semantic-subtask data
successor to π₀ with measurable generalization improvement
prior_art_notes: π₀.₅ is Physical Intelligence's open-world VLA (CoRL 2025 oral). 1-year-deep prior art on: open-world (new-home) zero-shot mobile manipulation, co-training across multi-robot + web + semantic subtask data, long-horizon (10+ minute) household task autonomy. **The most direct prior art for any commercial humanoid claim on 'works in any home out-of-the-box'** — Tesla Optimus, Figure, 1X NEO, Apptronik all market this generalization claim and now face 1-year-deep open-academic anticipation. Lineage: RT-1 → RT-2 → OpenVLA → π₀ → π₀.₅.

actuator_details: Real-time language-enhanced Gaussian-splatting SLAM. Fuses optimized Gaussian-splatting implementation with visual-language feature extraction via DINOv2 + learnable PCA-based feature compressor. Achieves 10+ fps on Replica dataset, 18 fps on ScanNet.
control_architecture: Provides real-time language-enhanced SLAM substrate.
creator: LEG-SLAM authors (per arXiv 2506.03073)
disclosure_citation: Authors per arXiv 2506.03073. 'LEG-SLAM: Real-Time Language-Enhanced Gaussian Splatting for SLAM'. arXiv:2506.03073, June 2025.
notable_capabilities: DINOv2 + PCA feature compression for language alignment
notes: DRAFT: full author list should be verified before promotion to commons-grade.
prior_art_notes: LEG-SLAM (June 2025) is a real-time language-enhanced GS-SLAM system. 11-month-deep prior art on: real-time fps-class language-aligned GS-SLAM, DINOv2 feature compression for compact per-Gaussian language encoding. Distinct from but contemporary with LEGO-SLAM (Nov 2025). Both feed the open-vocab GS-SLAM lineage that RADIO-ViPE compares against.

actuator_details: Wheel-legged hybrid robot with a distinctive front-leg configuration: **replaces conventional hip-roll DoF with hip-yaw DoFs on the front legs**, enabling efficient flat-surface movement while retaining complex-terrain adaptability. Mode-switching between legged and wheeled locomotion is the architectural focus.
control_architecture: Controllers for both legged and wheeled locomotion; seamless mode-transition.
creator: FLORES authors (per arXiv:2507.22345)
disclosure_citation: FLORES authors. 'FLORES: A Reconfigured Wheel-Legged Robot for Enhanced Steering and Adaptability'. arXiv:2507.22345, July 2025. Authors per arXiv listing.

prior_art_notes: FLORES is a contemporary (July 2025) wheel-legged-hybrid academic publication. Architecturally distinct from the STAR family by swapping hip-roll for hip-yaw on the front legs — a design choice that complements the DSTAR sprawl-tuned approach. Shields any commercial claim on hip-yaw front-leg wheel-leg-hybrid configurations and adds to the wheel-leg prior-art chain alongside DSTAR, RSTAR, STAR, AmphiSTAR. Specific authorship and venue per the arXiv preprint.

actuator_details: Online video pose engine: from raw uncalibrated video, estimates camera intrinsics, camera motion (poses), and dense near-metric depth maps. Supports pinhole, wide-angle, and 360° panoramic camera models. Solves a dense bundle adjustment with multi-constraint loss. Runs at 3-5 FPS on a single GPU. Outperforms MegaSAM and prior uncalibrated baselines by 18% / 50% on TUM / KITTI benchmarks.
control_architecture: Provides perception substrate (intrinsics + extrinsics + dense depth) for any robotic platform with monocular video. Released with a 96M-frame dataset of paired video + camera-pose + dense-depth annotations across internet videos, AI-generated videos, and panoramas — the largest such open dataset to date.
creator: NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab (nv-tlabs); multi-author
disclosure_citation: Huang, J., et al. (NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab + collaborators). 'ViPE: Video Pose Engine for 3D Geometric Perception'. arXiv:2508.10934, August 2025. Open-source release via nv-tlabs/vipe.
notable_capabilities: calibration-free metric depth and pose from unconstrained video
support for pinhole, wide-angle, and 360° cameras
3-5 FPS online operation on single GPU
18% / 50% improvement over MegaSAM on TUM / KITTI
prior_art_notes: ViPE is NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab's canonical Video Pose Engine, August 2025 arXiv. Sits **directly between DROID-SLAM (2021) and RADIO-ViPE (2026)** in the visual-SLAM lineage: it is RADIO-ViPE's explicit foundation per the round-10 paper's text ('we build upon ViPE [5]'). 9-month-deep open-permissive academic prior art for: calibration-free metric depth from uncalibrated video, dense bundle adjustment over heterogeneous camera models, online video pose estimation at 3-5 FPS. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on uncalibrated-camera onboard 3D perception. Plus the 96M-frame released dataset is itself prior art for any humanoid-vision data-curation IP.
sensing: single uncalibrated monocular RGB camera (input); produces metric depth + 6-DoF camera pose + intrinsics (output)

actuator_details: Anthropomorphic robot hand built **entirely from LEGO MINDSTORMS** components and standard LEGO bricks. Tendon-driven highly-underactuated five-finger hand based on the Pisa-IIT SoftHand and Tactile SoftHand-A lineage. **Dual motors driving an agonist-antagonist tendon pair on each finger** for active fine control. Finger motions synchronized via **soft synergies implemented with a differential mechanism using clutch gears** (a LEGO-friendly approximation of the SoftHand's textile-elastic synergies). 90% of the grip force of a professional 3D-printed SoftHand. <1 second open-close cycle.
control_architecture: LEGO MINDSTORMS hub controls dual motors per finger via standard LEGO interfaces. Designed for educational replication — full open-source build instructions and CAD files at lepora.com/EduSoftHand-A. Programmable via standard MINDSTORMS environment.
creator: Bristol Robotics Laboratory + Bristol Grammar School; Jared Lepora (16-yr student), Haoran Li, Efi Psomopoulou, Nathan F. Lepora
disclosure_citation: Lepora, J., Li, H., Psomopoulou, E., Lepora, N. F. 'Educational SoftHand-A: Building an Anthropomorphic Hand with Soft Synergies using LEGO® MINDSTORMS®'. arXiv:2510.15638, October 2025. Bristol Robotics Laboratory + Bristol Grammar School.
end_effector: five LEGO-built fingers with antagonistic tendons; differential clutch-gear synergy
notable_capabilities: anthropomorphic 5-finger hand from LEGO MINDSTORMS only
first author Jared Lepora was 16 at time of publication
prior_art_notes: Educational SoftHand-A is the LEGO MINDSTORMS instantiation of the Pisa-IIT SoftHand / Tactile SoftHand-A lineage (Oct 2025). 7-month-deep prior art for: differential clutch-gear synergy mechanism in LEGO bricks, agonist-antagonist tendon pair from a single dual-motor module, accessible educational reproduction of professional SoftHand-class designs. **Direct relevance for free-humanoid-platform hand v0.2** — the differential-synergy clutch-gear approach is documented open art that the v0.2 hand could adopt or explicitly diverge from. Together with pisa-iit-softhand, pisa-iit-softhand-2, and tactile-softhand-a-2025, the SoftHand synergy-mechanism lineage is now 11-year-deep continuous open academic publication (2014-2025) across four design generations.

actuator_details: First framework to achieve **real-time** open-vocabulary mapping within a 3DGS-based SLAM system. Scene-adaptive encoder-decoder distills high-dimensional language embeddings into a compact 16-dimensional per-Gaussian feature space. **Language-guided pruning** identifies semantic redundancy and reduces map Gaussian count by >60% while maintaining rendering quality.
control_architecture: Real-time open-vocabulary SLAM substrate. Open-source.
creator: Lab of AI and Robotics (per github.com/Lab-of-AI-and-Robotics/LEGO-SLAM)
disclosure_citation: Authors per arXiv 2511.16144. 'LEGO-SLAM: Language-Embedded Gaussian Optimization SLAM'. arXiv:2511.16144, November 2025. Lab of AI and Robotics.
notable_capabilities: 60%+ Gaussian count reduction via language-guided pruning
notes: DRAFT: full author list should be verified before promotion to commons-grade.
prior_art_notes: LEGO-SLAM (Nov 2025) is the first claimed real-time open-vocabulary GS-SLAM system. 6-month-deep prior art for: 16-dim language-feature compression in GS, language-guided Gaussian pruning. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on real-time onboard open-vocabulary scene mapping. Together with LEG-SLAM, LEGS, and SemGauss-SLAM, the open-vocab GS-SLAM corpus is now ~6-month to 14-month deep across five contemporary systems — fully covering the architectural surface of RADIO-ViPE's competitor table.

actuator_details: Most recent (2026) member of the STAR family. **Two independently-actuated four-bar extension mechanisms (FBEM)** + sprawl mechanism with extended range (sprawl angle θ ∈ [-105°, +105°]). 1150 g total mass. Each side has independent FBEM (αL, αR ∈ [-65°, +65°]) — asymmetric configurations enable **rolling sideways**, COM control in any direction, and 18 cm horizontal-gap traversal. 76 mm wheels. PLA+ 3D-printed body. Servo motors: 9imod DSC55MG (sprawl, 5.4 Nm), NEEBRC NB-H015 (FBEM, 2.29 Nm × 2), SA19 (drive, 1.77 Nm × 2). Raspberry Pi 4 B with Auto pHat driver. 2-cell LiPo + secondary battery for compute.
control_architecture: Five independent servo-motor DoF with kinematic + quasi-static force models published. Pre-programmed gait selection: turtle gait, sideways rolling, climbing, obstacle traversal. Wi-Fi + Bluetooth communication for remote operation or pre-programmed mission. Validated in experiment: 20 cm wall climbing (66% improvement over symmetric FBEM designs like RSTAR), uneven-terrain crossing, sideways rolling, self-recovery from stuck states.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; Tomer Siboni, Matan Coronel, David Zarrouk
disclosure_citation: Siboni, T., Coronel, M., Zarrouk, D. 'Design and Modeling of a Reconfigurable Robot: Decoupled STAR (DSTAR)'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters vol. 11 no. 1, January 2026, pp. 882-889. DOI: 10.1109/LRA.2025.3634888. Ben-Gurion University, Department of Mechanical Engineering / Bio-inspired Robotics Lab. Funded by Helmsley Charitable Trust + Marcus Endowment Fund.
notable_capabilities: 20 cm wall obstacle traversal (66% improvement over RSTAR)
sideways rolling via asymmetric FBEM configuration
operates on grass, dirt, stones, rubble per published experiments
prior_art_notes: DSTAR is the most recent STAR-family member, published IEEE RA-L January 2026. Establishes very-recent (4-month-deep) open-academic prior art for: decoupled-FBEM wheel-leg reconfigurable robotics, sideways rolling via asymmetric mechanical configuration, COM-shifting via independent left/right leg actuation, 18-20 cm obstacle traversal in palm-sized class. Directly anticipates free-humanoid-centaur's wheel-leg hybrid mode-switching commitment, free-humanoid-wheeled's obstacle-climbing requirement, and any commercial humanoid claim on reconfigurable wheel-leg architectures (including any mid-size extrapolation of DSTAR to humanoid scale). The full STAR family lineage (Berkeley original 2013 → Zarrouk RSTAR 2019 → AmphiSTAR 2023 → DSTAR 2026) provides 13-year-deep open-academic continuous publication coverage of every architectural element. Highly relevant for shoal dock-A wetland service: DSTAR's terrain-adaptation gait library is a published reference design for centaur-class wetland mode-transition.

actuator_details: Online semantic SLAM system. Calibration-free monocular RGB input — no prior camera intrinsics, no depth, no pose initialization required. Tightly couples multi-modal embeddings (RADIO agglomerative foundation model + SigLIP text encoder) with geometric scene information in a joint factor-graph optimization with adaptive robust kernels. Operates online at 8-10 FPS. State-of-the-art on TUM-RGBD dynamic benchmark (ATE 1.63 cm average vs. ViPE 2.17 / Dyna-SLAM 2.00).
aliases: Reduce All Domains Into One Video Pose Engine
control_architecture: Provides perception substrate for any robot with a camera. Outputs: calibrated camera poses, dense depth maps, dense PCA-compressed RADIO embeddings per pixel. Supports free-form natural-language object queries via SigLIP text-embedding matching against the dense map. Three-regime Barron-loss adaptive robust kernel jointly suppresses actively-moving agents and quasi-static displaced objects.
creator: ITMO University BE2R Lab; Nasser, Iumanov, Li, Popov, Mahmoud, Kolyubin
disclosure_citation: Nasser, Z., Iumanov, M., Li, T., Popov, M., Mahmoud, J., Kolyubin, S. 'RADIO-ViPE: Online Tightly Coupled Multi-Modal Fusion for Open-Vocabulary Semantic SLAM in Dynamic Environments'. arXiv:2604.26067v1, April 28, 2026. ITMO University, Biomechatronics and Energy-Efficient Robotics (BE2R) Lab, Saint Petersburg, Russia.
notable_capabilities: calibration-free (no camera intrinsics, no depth, no pose required)
SOTA on TUM-RGBD dynamic benchmark (ATE 1.63 cm)
prior_art_notes: RADIO-ViPE is the most recent and architecturally complete online open-vocabulary semantic SLAM system. April 2026 arXiv preprint; 9 days before this corpus entry. Establishes very-recent (sub-1-week) open-academic prior art for: calibration-free monocular semantic SLAM, tightly-coupled multi-modal fusion (RADIO + SigLIP + geometric BA), adaptive-kernel dynamic-scene robustness, online operation at 8-10 FPS. Directly shields any commercial humanoid claim on: 'onboard semantic scene understanding from monocular video' (Tesla Optimus, Figure 02, 1X NEO, Apptronik Apollo, etc. all face this), 'language-grounded robotic perception in dynamic environments', 'calibration-free humanoid camera deployment'. The TUM-RGBD ATE comparison table in Table II of the paper enumerates the prior art — RADIO-ViPE outperforms Dyna-SLAM, DLD-SLAM, V3D-SLAM, DGS-SLAM, RoDyn-SLAM, DynaMON, ViPE — every one of which is itself open-academic prior art for humanoid perception. Lineage: ORB-SLAM3 (geometric baseline) → DROID-SLAM (dense differentiable) → ViPE (Princeton in-the-wild metric depth) → RADIO-ViPE (ITMO open-vocab + calibration-free).
sensing: single uncalibrated monocular RGB camera (the entire input); produces depth + pose + dense semantic embeddings as output
sources: Foundation models: NVIDIA RADIO (Ranzinger et al. 2024), SigLIP (Zhai et al. ICCV 2023).
